definition_zh: 同意；允许；赞同；许可
definition_en: to agree to something, or official permission for something to happen
core_image: 合同末尾，笔尖在签名栏上停了一秒才落下
scene: 医生把手术同意书推到家属面前，等他们点头。 Her parents consented to the trip.
sceneCN: 这里 consent 指「同意」（第 1 个义项：表示许可）；句意是她的父母同意了这趟旅行。

senses.title: Say yes
senses.definition: to agree to something or give permission for it
senses.definitionCN: 同意某事或给予许可
senses.example: She consented to the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 她同意接受采访。
senses.why: Two wills meet, and one of them stops resisting.
senses.whyCN: 两种意愿相遇，其中一种不再抵抗。

senses.title: Official permission
senses.definition: official agreement that allows something to happen
senses.definitionCN: 允许某事发生的正式同意
senses.example: The builder needs written consent from the owner.
senses.exampleCN: 施工方需要业主的书面同意。
senses.why: A spoken yes fades, so the law asks it to leave a mark.
senses.whyCN: 口头答应会消散，所以法律要求它留下痕迹。

senses.title: A shared view
senses.definition: general agreement among a group, an older and rarer sense
senses.definitionCN: 一群人的普遍一致，是较古老且少用的义项
senses.example: By common consent the plan was dropped.
senses.exampleCN: 经大家一致同意，这个计划被放弃了。
senses.why: When many feelings move the same way, no vote is needed.
senses.whyCN: 当许多人的感受朝同一方向走，就不需要投票了。

intro.en: Consent comes from Latin consentire, to feel together, from com-, together, and sentire, to feel.
intro.cn: consent 来自拉丁语 consentire，意为一起感受，由 com-（一起）与 sentire（感觉）构成。

items.en: Sentire meant to feel, perceive or think.
items.cn: sentire 意为感觉、察觉或思考。

items.en: Consentire meant to feel the same way as another.
items.cn: consentire 意为与另一个人感受相同。

items.en: The noun consensus named that shared feeling.
items.cn: 名词 consensus 指这种共同的感受。

items.en: Old French consentir carried the sense of agreeing.
items.cn: 古法语 consentir 带有同意的含义。

items.en: English consent first meant to agree or be of one mind.
items.cn: 英语 consent 最初指同意或心意一致。

items.en: It now also names formal permission in law and medicine.
items.cn: 如今它也指法律与医疗中的正式许可。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sound of consent, and the meaning group names other ways of saying yes.
note.cn: 形近组与 consent 读音相近，近义组列出其他表示答应的说法。

entries.definition: an opinion shared by most people
formal agreement to a plan
to feel angry about something unfair
to have the same opinion
to officially accept something
the right to do something given by someone

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from two people feeling the same way, then move to a signature and to a room that agrees without voting.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从两个人感受相同开始，再到一个签名，最后到不用投票就一致的房间。

normal.en: Con- is together and sent- is feel, so consent is to feel along with someone.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，sent- 是感觉，consent 就是跟着对方一起感受。

normal.en: A nod is the shortest contract in the world.
normal.cn: 一个点头，是世界上最简短的合同。

normal.en: Consent given in writing is a yes you cannot take back easily.
normal.cn: 写下来的同意，是难以轻易收回的答应。

normal.en: No consent, no entry: the same rule for doors and for bodies.
normal.cn: 没有同意就不许进：门如此，人也是如此。

normal.en: When everyone consents, the meeting ends early.
normal.cn: 大家都同意时，会就提前散了。

abstract.en: Picture a pen hovering above a line.
abstract.cn: 想象一支笔在一条横线上方悬着。

abstract.en: Picture two heads nodding at the same second.
abstract.cn: 想象两个头在同一秒点下去。

abstract.en: Picture a door opened from the inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门从里面被打开。

examples.en: He consented to the search of his bag.
examples.cn: 他同意接受检查他的包。

examples.en: No one may enter the site without consent.
examples.cn: 未经许可，任何人不得进入场地。

examples.en: Her consent was given in writing.
examples.cn: 她的同意是以书面形式给出的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 consent 记成 con（一起）加 sent（感觉）：两个人感觉到一起去了，自然就点头同意。

root: 源自拉丁语 consentire（com 一起 + sentire 感觉），本义是感受相同，后指同意、赞同与正式许可。

sensesIntro.en: From two feelings moving as one, to a signed permission, and finally to a whole group thinking alike.
sensesIntro.cn: 从两种感受合而为一，到签下的许可，最后到整个群体想法一致。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two heads nodding at the very same moment.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个头在同一瞬间点下去。

branches.en: The verb is the act of agreeing or allowing.
branches.cn: 动词义项就是同意或允许的动作。

branches.en: The noun sense is the permission that remains on record.
branches.cn: 名词义项是留在记录里的那份许可。

branches.en: The older sense is a group feeling the same way.
branches.cn: 较古老的义项是一群人感受相同。

branches.en: Saying yes and the paper that proves it are one process.
branches.cn: 说出同意与证明它的那张纸，是同一个过程。

branches.en: Both rest on people finding that their feelings match.
branches.cn: 两者都建立在人们发现彼此感受相合之上。

intro.en: Consent is built on Latin com-, together, plus sentire, to feel.
intro.cn: consent 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 sentire（感觉）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin feel base sent- also appears in assent, dissent, resent and sensation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的感觉词基 sent- 也出现在 assent、dissent、resent 与 sensation 中。

items.meaning: to feel the same and agree

items.exampleCN: 这是一个双方同意的决定。
两位法官写下了反对意见。

items.meaning: to feel anger again and again
items.exampleCN: 她对那条不公平的规定感到愤恨。

items.example: A cold sensation spread down his arm.
items.exampleCN: 一阵冰凉的感觉顺着手臂蔓延。

definition_zh: 复印件；影印件；复印；影印
definition_en: a copy of a page or picture made by a machine that scans the original and prints it again; to make such a copy
core_image: 绿灯从纸页下面扫过，原件旁边立刻多出一张几乎一样的纸
scene: 出入境大厅的窗口前，办事员把护照放到玻璃板上，按下按钮。 The clerk made a photocopy of my passport and handed it back with the receipt.
sceneCN: 这里是「复印件」（第 1 个义项：机器复制出来的纸本）；句意为办事员复印了我的护照，连同收据一起递还。图中的玻璃板、亮起的扫描条和吐出的纸页正是复印机的动作。

derivatives.zh: photocopy 去 y 加 -er，指执行复印这件事的机器，义为「复印机」
photocopy 加 -ing，把动作变成过程名词，义为「复印；复印业务」
photocopy 加 -able，义为「可以复印的」，教材上常见

senses.title: A machine-made copy of a page
senses.definition: a copy of a document or picture produced by a machine that scans the original and prints the same image again
senses.definitionCN: 用机器扫描原件、再把同样的图像印出来而得到的文件或图片副本
senses.example: Keep a photocopy of the contract in the drawer.
senses.exampleCN: 把合同的复印件放在抽屉里。
senses.why: Photo- adds the idea of an image and copy adds the Latin sense of one more unit, so the machine never writes anything new; it multiplies an existing image onto a second sheet.
senses.whyCN: photo- 带来「影像」，copy 的拉丁本义是「多出一份」，所以复印机并不写新内容，只是把已有的影像再放到一张纸上，让它多出一份。

senses.title: To reproduce a page by machine
senses.definition: to make a copy of a document or picture with a copying machine
senses.definitionCN: 用复印机复制文件或图片
senses.example: Could you photocopy these pages before the meeting?
senses.exampleCN: 你能在开会前把这些页面复印一下吗？
senses.why: English turns product nouns into verbs without any suffix, so the same spelling names both the sheet on the tray and the act that put it there.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把指成品的名词直接用作动词，不加词尾；于是同一个拼写既指托盘里的那张纸，也指把它做出来的那个动作。

intro.en: Photocopy joins a Greek element for light to a Latin word for plenty; the machine later changed its chemistry while the old name stayed.
intro.cn: photocopy 把希腊语表示「光」的成分和拉丁语表示「充足」的词接在一起；后来机器的成像原理换了，名字却留了下来。

items.en: Phos, with the genitive photos, meant light, and the combining form photo- was already used by nineteenth-century science for things produced by light.
items.cn: phos 的属格是 photos，意为光；photo- 这个组合形式在十九世纪科学里已用来指由光产生的东西。

items.en: Copia meant abundance and supply; through Old French copie it became English copy, one more unit of a text.
items.cn: copia 意为充足、供应；经古法语 copie 进入英语成为 copy，指文本多出来的一份。

items.en: Photo- and copy were joined in English for a reproduction made by a photographic process, at first a photograph of a page.
items.cn: 英语把 photo- 与 copy 拼合，指用照相工艺做出的复制品，最初就是一页文件的照片。

items.en: When office machines could expose paper to light and fix toner on it, the same word moved to the plain-paper copy people still make today.
items.cn: 当办公机器能让纸张曝光并把墨粉固定上去，同一个词就转指今天仍在制作的普通纸复印件。

items.en: Photocopy now covers the paper and the act, while photocopier names the machine and photocopying names the service.
items.cn: 现代英语里 photocopy 兼指纸本与动作，photocopier 指机器，photocopying 指这项业务。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the two halves of the word, Greek photo- and Latin copy; the near-meaning group collects other words for a second version of a page.
note.cn: 形近组沿着这个词的两半展开，希腊语的 photo- 与拉丁语的 copy；近义组收其他表示「纸页的第二份」的词。

entries.definition: The machine that does the copying, built with -er on the same base.
entries.definitionCN: 执行复印的机器，在同一词干上加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: The process or service of reproducing pages, marked by -ing.
entries.definitionCN: 复制纸页的过程或业务，由 -ing 标记。

entries.definition: A camera picture made by light; it shares photo- but ends in the Greek -graph, not in copy.
entries.definitionCN: 用相机拍下、由光成像的画面；同用 photo-，结尾却是希腊语的 -graph，不是 copy。

entries.definition: One duplicate of a text or image, the Latin half that photocopy carries.
entries.definitionCN: 文本或图像的一份副本，是 photocopy 所带的拉丁语那一半。

entries.definition: An exact second version of something that already exists.
entries.definitionCN: 已有事物完全一样的第二份。

entries.definition: A copy of an image or text, often made for printing or display.
entries.definitionCN: 图像或文本的复制品，常为印刷或展示而做。

entries.definition: A page a printer produces from a computer file rather than from a paper original.
entries.definitionCN: 打印机从电脑文件而非纸质原件输出的一页。

entries.definition: To turn a page into a digital image, the step that often comes before copies are made.
entries.definitionCN: 把纸页变成数字图像，常是复制之前的步骤。

normalIntro.en: The word is built from two real halves, and each half explains part of what the machine does.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由两个真实的成分拼成，每一半都解释了机器所做事情的一部分。

normal.en: Photo- gives the image and copy gives the extra one, so a photocopy is an image that has been multiplied.
normal.cn: photo- 给出影像，copy 给出多出来的一份，所以 photocopy 就是被复制了一份的影像。

normal.en: The machine, not the person, is the photocopier: -er here marks a device, as it does in printer and scanner.
normal.cn: 机器而不是人才是 photocopier：这里的 -er 标记器械，和 printer、scanner 一样。

normal.en: Photocopying keeps -ing for the activity, so a photocopying service sells the act, not the paper.
normal.cn: photocopying 用 -ing 表示活动，所以复印服务卖的是这项动作，而不是纸张。

normal.en: Modern machines use toner and static electricity, but light still exposes the page, so the photo- half is not a lie.
normal.cn: 现代机器用墨粉和静电，但纸页仍靠光曝光，所以 photo- 那一半并没有说谎。

normal.en: Photocopy has no -graph: its second half is Latin copy, which is exactly what separates it from photograph.
normal.cn: photocopy 没有 -graph：后半截是拉丁语 copy，这正是它与 photograph 的分界。

abstract.en: A photocopy is a stand-in that can be read, filed and lost without anyone touching the original.
abstract.cn: 复印件是一个替身：它可以被阅读、归档、遗失，而原件始终无人碰过。

abstract.en: The name still promises light although the machine mostly moves powder, which is how words quietly age.
abstract.cn: 名字仍在承诺「光」，机器却主要在搬运粉末，词语就是这样悄悄老去的。

abstract.en: Two identical pages raise a small question: which one is the document and which one is only a trace of it.
abstract.cn: 两张一样的纸会引出一个问题：哪一张是文件本身，哪一张只是它的痕迹。

examples.en: Keep a photocopy of the contract in the drawer.
examples.cn: 把合同的复印件放在抽屉里。

examples.en: Could you photocopy these pages before the meeting?
examples.cn: 你能在开会前把这些页面复印一下吗？

examples.en: She photocopied the whole file twice.
examples.cn: 她把整份档案复印了两遍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「否头拷皮」——把原件的外皮拷一份到新纸上；记住 photocopy 是复印件，也能当动词「复印」。

root: 希腊语 phos/photos（光）+ 拉丁语 copia（充足、副本，经古法语 copie 入英语）；photo- 只借了「光」，后半截 copy 并非希腊语 -graph。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a second copy produced through an image-forming machine; the senses divide only by whether the word names the paper or the act.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是通过成像机器多出来的一份副本；两个义项只在于是指那张纸，还是指复印这个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bar of green light sliding under a page while an identical sheet slides out below.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道绿光从纸页下扫过，下面同时滑出另一张一模一样的纸。

branches.en: a passport copy folded into a coat pocket
branches.cn: 折进外套口袋的护照复印件

branches.en: a hand pressing the copy button twice
branches.cn: 一只手连按两下复印键

branches.en: the act ending in a warm stack of paper
branches.cn: 动作结束于一叠还带着温度的纸

branches.en: a class handout identical to the teacher's page
branches.cn: 与老师那页一模一样的课堂讲义

branches.en: copying a whole file before a meeting
branches.cn: 开会前把整份档案复印一遍

intro.en: The word stands on a Greek element for light and a Latin noun for plenty, and English welds them without a linking vowel change.
intro.cn: 这个词站在希腊语表示「光」的成分和拉丁语表示「充足」的名词上，英语把两者直接焊在一起。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: a machine-made copy; to make one

definition_zh: 产生；发电；引起
definition_en: to produce energy, to cause something to begin, or to create data or material
core_image: 水坝的水流推动涡轮机发出电来
scene: 大坝发电。 The dam generates electricity.
sceneCN: 这里 generate 是「产生；发电」（第 1 个义项）；句意：大坝发电。

senses.title: Produce energy
senses.definition: to produce power, heat, or another form of energy
senses.definitionCN: 产生动力、热量或其他形式的能量
senses.example: The dam generates electricity.
senses.exampleCN: 大坝发电。
senses.why: This is the basic physical sense of producing power.
senses.whyCN: 这是产生动力的基本实体义项。

senses.title: Cause to begin
senses.definition: to cause a feeling, reaction, or situation
senses.definitionCN: 引起某种情绪、反应或状况
senses.example: The news generated a lot of interest.
senses.exampleCN: 这条消息引起了很大兴趣。
senses.why: The word extends from energy to effects.
senses.whyCN: 词义从能量扩展到效果。

senses.title: Create material
senses.definition: to create data, text, or other material by a process
senses.definitionCN: 通过某种过程创建数据、文本或其他材料
senses.example: The program generates a report each week.
senses.exampleCN: 这个程序每周生成一份报告。
senses.why: Machines and software are said to generate output.
senses.whyCN: 机器和软件被说成生成输出。

intro.en: Generate comes from Latin generare, to bring into being.
intro.cn: generate 来自拉丁语 generare，意为使产生。

items.en: Genus meant birth, kind, or family.
items.cn: genus 意为出生、种类或家族。

items.en: Generare meant to beget or produce.
items.cn: generare 意为生育或产生。

items.en: English adopted generate for producing something.
items.cn: 英语借入 generate，表示产生某物。

items.en: Industry gave it the sense of producing power.
items.cn: 工业赋予它产生动力的意思。

items.en: Computing extended it to creating data and text.
items.cn: 计算机领域把它扩展到创建数据和文本。

note.en: Generate is compared with look-alike words and verbs of producing.
note.cn: 把 generate 与形近词以及表示产生的动词作比较。

entries.definition: willing to give freely
shared by a whole group
friendly and cheerful
to make or grow something
to make something new
to give a result or product

normalIntro.en: To generate is to set something into being, whether power, feeling, or data.
normalIntro.cn: generate 就是让某物产生，无论是动力、感受还是数据。

normal.en: The dam generates electricity.
normal.cn: 大坝发电。

normal.en: The news generated a lot of interest.
normal.cn: 这条消息引起了很大兴趣。

normal.en: The program generates a report each week.
normal.cn: 这个程序每周生成一份报告。

normal.en: Friction generates heat.
normal.cn: 摩擦产生热量。

normal.en: The new factory will generate jobs.
normal.cn: 新工厂将创造就业机会。

abstract.en: Every action generates a consequence somewhere.
abstract.cn: 每个行动都会在某处产生后果。

abstract.en: A single idea can generate a whole industry.
abstract.cn: 一个想法可以催生整个产业。

abstract.en: Energy is never made; it only changes form.
abstract.cn: 能量从未被凭空制造，只是改变了形式。

examples.en: The dam generates electricity.
examples.cn: 大坝发电。

examples.en: The news generated a lot of interest.
examples.cn: 这条消息引起了很大兴趣。

examples.en: The program generates a report each week.
examples.cn: 这个程序每周生成一份报告。

dict_mnemonic.text: generate 与 generation、generator 同根；generate electricity 是「发电」，generate income 是「创造收入」。

root: 拉丁语 generare（生育、产生），源于 genus（出生、种类），核心义「使之产生」。

sensesIntro.en: Generate means to produce energy, to cause a feeling or situation, or to create data and material.
sensesIntro.cn: generate 意为产生能量、引起情绪或状况，或创建数据和材料。

core.en: Bringing something into being.
core.cn: 使某物产生。

branches.en: Water turns a turbine into power.
branches.cn: 水流转动涡轮产生电力。

branches.en: News starts a reaction in people.
branches.cn: 消息在人们中间引发反应。

branches.en: A program makes a fresh report.
branches.cn: 程序生成一份新的报告。

branches.en: Physical power and social effect both begin somewhere.
branches.cn: 物理动力与社会效果都有其起点。

branches.en: Output can be feeling or data.
branches.cn: 产出可以是感受，也可以是数据。

intro.en: Generate builds words for production, machines, and new output.
intro.cn: generate 构成表示产生、机器和新生输出的词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root generare means to beget or produce.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词根 generare 意为生育或产生。

items.example: The panels generate power all day.
The engine generates a lot of heat.
items.exampleCN: 这台发动机产生大量热量。

items.meaning: the act of producing or a group born together

items.example: The generator kept the lights on.
The land generates income for the village.
items.exampleCN: 这片土地为村庄创造收入。

latinEntries.example: Generare is the Latin verb behind generate.
latinEntries.exampleCN: generare 是 generate 背后的拉丁语动词。

definition_zh: 一瞥；瞥一眼；浏览
definition_en: a quick look, to look quickly, or to read through briefly
core_image: 走路时目光迅速扫过街边的一扇窗
scene: 她朝窗外瞥了一眼。 She glanced at the window.
sceneCN: 这里 glance 是「瞥一眼」（第 2 个义项）；句意：她朝窗外瞥了一眼。

senses.title: A quick look
senses.definition: a short look at something
senses.definitionCN: 朝某物匆匆看一眼
senses.example: She took a quick glance at the clock.
senses.exampleCN: 她匆匆看了一眼钟。
senses.why: The noun names the brief act itself.
senses.whyCN: 名词直接命名这个短暂的动作。

senses.title: To look quickly
senses.definition: to look at something for a short time

definition_zh: 不可避免的；必然发生的；必然的；不可避免的事
definition_en: certain to happen and impossible to avoid or prevent

senses.title: Impossible to avoid
senses.definition: impossible to escape or prevent, no matter what one does
senses.definitionCN: 无论怎么做都无法逃脱或阻止
senses.example: With the road flooded, a delay was inevitable.
senses.exampleCN: 道路被淹，延误已无法避免。
senses.why: The word is the negation of evitable 'avoidable'. Latin evitabilis comes from evitare 'to shun'. To call something inevitable is to say that every route of avoidance is closed.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 evitable“可避免的”的否定式。拉丁语 evitabilis 来自 evitare“躲避”。称某事 inevitable，就是说每一条躲避的路都已关闭。

senses.title: Certain to happen
senses.titleCN: 必然发生：时间到了就会来
senses.definition: sure to happen at some point, even if the exact time is unknown
senses.definitionCN: 在某个时点必定发生，即使具体时间未知
senses.example: Some conflict is inevitable when two teams share one budget.
senses.exampleCN: 两个团队共用一份预算时，某些冲突必然发生。
senses.why: Avoidance concerns a person's power; certainty concerns the event's arrival. The same word covers both because a thing that cannot be prevented is also a thing that will certainly come.
senses.whyCN: “躲避”关乎人有没有能力；“必然”关乎事件会不会到来。同一个词覆盖两者，因为无法被阻止的事，也就是必定会来的事。

senses.title: Logically necessary
senses.titleCN: 逻辑必然：由前提必然推出
senses.definition: following necessarily from the premises or the stated conditions
senses.definitionCN: 由前提或已陈述的条件必然推出
senses.example: If every voter must be counted, a recount is inevitable.
senses.exampleCN: 如果每一张选票都必须被计入，重新计票就是必然的。
senses.why: Logic turns the word from physical prevention to entailment: given the premises, no other conclusion can be drawn. This is necessity in the strict sense.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑把这个词从“物理上阻止”转为“蕴含”：给定前提，就得不出别的结论。这是严格意义上的必然性。

senses.title: Predictable and routine
senses.titleCN: 意料之中：老一套、不出所料
senses.definition: so habitual or expected that it can be predicted with confidence
senses.definitionCN: 如此习惯或可预期，以至于能很有把握地预测
senses.example: The inevitable question came: who will pay for it?
senses.exampleCN: 那个意料之中的问题来了：谁来付钱？
senses.why: Here necessity is weakened into habit. The event is not logically forced, but experience makes it feel as if it could not be otherwise.
senses.whyCN: 这里“必然”被弱化成习惯。事件并非逻辑上被迫发生，但经验让它感觉仿佛不可能有别的样子。

senses.title: An unavoidable event (noun)
senses.definition: as a noun, an event or outcome that cannot be avoided
senses.definitionCN: 作名词时，指无法避免的事件或结果
senses.example: They prepared for the inevitable rather than pretending it would not come.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为不可避免的事做准备，而不是假装它不会来。
senses.why: The adjective became a noun by 1850. English often turns an adjective into a name for the thing that carries the quality, so 'the inevitable' is 'that which is inevitable'.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词在 1850 年前已可作名词。英语常把形容词变成具有该性质之物的名称，因此 the inevitable 就是“那个不可避免的东西”。

senses.title: Death, as the inevitable
senses.titleCN: 委婉语：死亡这一必然结局
senses.definition: in euphemistic usage, death, viewed as the one event no one escapes
senses.definitionCN: 委婉用法中指死亡，被视为无人能逃脱的那件事
senses.example: When the inevitable finally came, the family was ready.
senses.exampleCN: 当那不可避免的结局终于到来时，家人已经做好了准备。
senses.why: The noun use allows speakers to avoid the word death. The euphemism works because the adjective already says everything: it cannot be avoided, so it need not be named.
senses.whyCN: 名词用法让说话者避开“死亡”一词。这个委婉语之所以成立，是因为形容词已经说尽了一切：它无法避免，因此不必点名。

senses.title: Philosophically unchangeable
senses.titleCN: 哲学意义上的不可更改
senses.definition: in philosophy, describing what cannot be otherwise, especially under determinism or fate
senses.definitionCN: 哲学中描述不可能另有状态的事，尤在决定论或宿命论语境下
senses.example: The argument claims that every choice is inevitable in advance.
senses.exampleCN: 该论证声称，每一个选择事先都是必然的。
senses.why: Philosophy pushes the word to its limit: not merely unpreventable by us, but fixed in the structure of causes. Here inevitable approaches 'fated'.
senses.whyCN: 哲学把这个词推到极限：不只是我们无法阻止，而是在因果结构中被固定。此处 inevitable 接近“命中注定”。

senses.title: Unavoidably accompanying something
senses.titleCN: 必然伴随：代价无法剥离
senses.definition: always present as a cost or side effect of a chosen course
senses.definitionCN: 作为某项选择过程的代价或副作用而始终存在
senses.example: Some noise is inevitable in any city-centre flat.
senses.exampleCN: 任何市中心的公寓都不可避免地会有一些噪音。
senses.why: The word can attach to a drawback rather than an event: if you take the benefit, the accompanying cost cannot be separated from it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也可以附着在缺点而非事件上：如果你要那份好处，伴随的代价就无法从中剥离。

intro.en: Inevitable is a Latin negative built on evitare 'to avoid'. Its first English uses were about unavoidable outcomes; the noun and the death euphemism are 19c developments. The deepest origin of vitare is uncertain.
intro.cn: inevitable 是建立在 evitare“避开”之上的拉丁否定式。它最早的英语用法指无法避免的结果；名词用法与指死亡的委婉语是 19 世纪的发展。vitare 的更早来源并不确定。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'unavoidable, that cannot be evaded'. The earliest context is general predication, not yet a fixed noun.
items.cn: 最早在英语中记录为“无法避免、无法躲开的”。最早的语境是一般性陈述，尚未固定为名词。

items.en: Inevitabilis is in- 'not' + evitabilis 'avoidable'. The prefix is privative: it denies the ability named by the adjective.
items.cn: inevitabilis 是 in-“不”+ evitabilis“可避免的”。这个前缀是否定性的：它否定形容词所指的能力。

items.en: Evitare 'to shun, avoid' is ex- 'out of' + vitare 'shun'. The ex- marks moving out of the way; the whole verb pictures stepping aside from something.
items.cn: evitare“躲避、避开”是 ex-“离开”+ vitare“躲避”。ex- 表示移出原来的路径；整个动词描绘的正是从某物旁边让开。

items.en: The further origin of vitare is uncertain. Standard etymological references treat it as unclear; older guesses linking it to via 'way' or to a root meaning 'away' are not established. Marked source uncertain.
items.cn: vitare 的更早来源不确定。通行词源资料将其视为不清楚；把它联系到 via“道路”或某个意为“离开”的词根的旧猜测并未得到确认。故标为来源不确定。

items.en: The noun use 'an inevitable thing' is recorded by 1850. English can nominalize the adjective with the definite article: the inevitable.
items.cn: 名词用法“不可避免之事”在 1850 年前已有记录。英语可用定冠词把形容词名词化：the inevitable。

items.en: The inevitable becomes a euphemism for death, and inevitability a key term in philosophy and in narratives of history. Inevitably spreads as the everyday adverb.
items.cn: the inevitable 成为指死亡的委婉语，inevitability 成为哲学与历史叙事中的关键术语。inevitably 则作为日常副词广泛使用。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the evit- root; the near-meaning group separates 'cannot be avoided' from 'certain' and 'fated'.
note.cn: 形近组共享 evit- 词根；近义组区分“无法避免”“确定”与“命中注定”。

entries.definition: impossible to escape or evade. It stresses being trapped rather than the certainty of an event.

normalIntro.cn: 真实前缀与真实对比；这里的 in- 是“不”，evitable 是被否定的肯定词。

normal.en: in- 'not' + evitable 'avoidable': inevitable is simply the denial of avoidability.
normal.cn: in-“不”+ evitable“可避免的”：inevitable 就是否定“可避免性”。

normal.en: Evitare contains vitare 'shun', not vita 'life'; the word has nothing to do with life.
normal.cn: evitare 含 vitare“躲避”，不是 vita“生命”；这个词与“生命”无关。

normal.en: Compare evitable, inevitably and inevitability: one root, one negative prefix, three parts of speech.
normal.cn: 对比 evitable、inevitably、inevitability：一个词根、一个否定前缀、三种词性。

normal.en: -able means 'can be': evitable = can be avoided; inevitable = cannot be avoided.
normal.cn: -able 意为“能被”：evitable＝能被避免；inevitable＝不能被避免。
