examples.cn: 鉴于人手短缺，一些延误是不可避免的。

examples.en: The committee treated the merger as inevitable and stopped debating it.
examples.cn: 委员会把合并视为必然，便停止了争论。

examples.en: Inevitably, the cheapest option failed first.
examples.cn: 不可避免地，最便宜的方案最先失败。

dict_mnemonic.text: “因爱我·逃不脱”——因为爱，我逃不脱，结局不可避免 → inevitable 不可避免的

root: 源自拉丁语 inevitabilis“无法避免的”，由 in-“不”+ evitabilis“可避免的”构成；evitabilis 来自 evitare“避开”，由 ex-“出、离开”+ vitare“躲避”构成。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of inevitable, all built on one closed route. The closure may be physical, logical, habitual, philosophical, or the final closure of death.
sensesIntro.cn: inevitable 的八个义项都建立在“一条被封闭的路”上。这种封闭可以是物理的、逻辑的、习惯性的、哲学性的，也可以是死亡那最后的封闭。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: every side road is closed, so only one direction remains.
core.cn: 核心意象：每条岔路都被封住，只剩一个方向。

branches.en: NO ESCAPE AND CERTAINTY: what cannot be prevented is also what will surely arrive.
branches.cn: 无路可躲与确定：无法被阻止的事，也必定会到来。

branches.en: NECESSITY: premises force a conclusion; a causal system leaves no alternative.
branches.cn: 必然性：前提迫使结论成立；因果系统不留别的可能。

branches.en: HABIT: experience makes an outcome feel fixed before it happens.
branches.cn: 习惯：经验让某个结果在发生前就显得已经固定。

branches.en: THE THING ITSELF: an unavoidable event, or a cost that cannot be separated from a benefit.
branches.cn: 事物本身：一个无法避免的事件，或无法与好处剥离的代价。

branches.en: DEATH: the one appointment no diplomacy can cancel.
branches.cn: 死亡：唯一无法通过任何周旋取消的约定。

intro.en: Inevitable is in- 'not' + evitabilis 'avoidable', from evitare 'avoid'. English adds -ably, -ability, -ableness, and keeps the rare positive evitable.
intro.cn: inevitable 是 in-“不”+ evitabilis“可避免的”，后者来自 evitare“避开”。英语加 -ably、-ability、-ableness，并保留少见的肯定形式 evitable。

latinIntro.en: Latin evitare 'shun, avoid' (ex- + vitare) and evitabilis 'avoidable'. Note that vitare is not vita 'life', though the forms look close.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族是 evitare“躲避、避开”（ex- + vitare）与 evitabilis“可避免的”。注意 vitare 不是 vita“生命”，尽管词形相近。

items.meaning: in a way that cannot be avoided; necessarily
items.example: Inevitably, the news spread faster than the official statement.
items.exampleCN: 不可避免地，消息比官方声明传得更快。

items.meaning: the quality of being impossible to avoid
items.meaningCN: 必然性；不可避免的性质
items.example: The report questions the inevitability of the collapse.
items.exampleCN: 这份报告质疑崩溃的必然性。

items.meaning: the state of being unavoidable (less common)
items.meaningCN: 不可避免的状态（较少用）
items.example: The inevitableness of the change silenced the room.
items.exampleCN: 变革的不可避免让全场沉默。

items.meaningCN: 可避免的；能够被躲开的
items.example: The loss was evitable, but no one acted in time.
items.exampleCN: 这次损失本可避免，但没人及时行动。

items.meaning: in a way that can be avoided (rare)
items.example: Such errors are evitably caused by haste.
items.exampleCN: 这类错误是可以通过不急躁而避免的。

items.example: Philosophers still debate the evitability of the outcome.
items.exampleCN: 哲学家仍在争论这一结果是否可避免。

items.meaning: impossible to avoid; a native-prefix parallel to inevitable
items.meaningCN: 无法避免的；用本族语前缀构成的同义平行形式
items.example: The overlap in duties was unavoidable.
items.exampleCN: 职责上的重叠无法避免。

items.meaning: in a way that cannot be avoided
items.example: The meeting unavoidably ran into lunchtime.
items.exampleCN: 会议不可避免地拖到了午饭时间。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 可避免的；能够被躲开的
躲避；避开（更早来源不确定）

definition_zh: 美德；德行；优点；长处；效力；贞操
definition_en: a good quality of character, or a useful strength in a thing
core_image: 一个人把力气用在正处，站得笔直
scene: 毕业典礼上，老校长没有讲成绩，只讲了诚实与耐心这两件事。 Patience was the one virtue the job truly required.
sceneCN: 这里 virtue 是「美德」（第 1 个义项：品格中的善）；句意为耐心是这份工作真正需要的一种美德。把力气用在正处、站得笔直的那个人，就是这个词的形象。

pos.zh: 美德；德行；优点；长处；效力

collocations.zh: 化不得已为美德；将就办事

derivatives.zh: virtue 加 -ous 构成，义为「有德行的；正直的」
同出拉丁词根 virtus，义为「几乎；实际上」
同根形容词，义为「实质上的；虚拟的」
同根名词，义为「精湛技艺」

senses.title: A good quality of character
senses.definition: a quality in a person that is good and worth praising, such as honesty or courage
senses.definitionCN: 个人身上值得赞许的善的品质，如诚实、勇气
senses.example: Patience was the one virtue the job truly required.
senses.exampleCN: 耐心是这份工作真正需要的一种美德。
senses.why: Latin virtus first meant manly strength and courage, and the word slowly moved from strength of body to strength of character used well.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 virtus 最初意为男子气概的力量与勇气，这个词慢慢从身体之力转到用得其所的品格之力。

senses.title: A good point in a thing
senses.definition: a useful strength or good feature in an object, a plan or a method
senses.definitionCN: 物体、方案或方法中可取的长处
senses.example: The chief virtue of the old car is that it never breaks down.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆旧车最大的优点是它从不坏。
senses.why: If a person can have good qualities, so can a plan; the word applies to anything with strengths worth naming.
senses.whyCN: 人能有好品质，方案也能，于是这个词用于任何值得称道的长处。

senses.title: Power to produce an effect
senses.definition: the power of something, such as a medicine or a herb, to act as it should
senses.definitionCN: 药物或草药等发挥应有作用的力量
senses.example: The virtue of the plant lies in its bitter root.
senses.exampleCN: 这种植物的效力在于它苦涩的根。
senses.why: Older medicine spoke of the virtue of a herb, meaning its active strength, which is strength again, now inside a plant.
senses.whyCN: 早期医学讲草药的 virtue，指它的有效之力，还是「力量」，只是转到了植物身上。

senses.title: Chastity, especially of a woman
senses.definition: in older use, chastity, chiefly spoken of a woman
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法，指贞洁，主要用来指女性
senses.example: The old play makes her virtue a matter of public talk.
senses.exampleCN: 那部老戏把她的贞洁写成众人议论的事。
senses.why: A narrow set of rules once gathered around the word, so one particular virtue became the virtue; modern use keeps it mainly historical.
senses.whyCN: 一套狭窄的规矩曾围着这个词，于是某一种美德就成了 the virtue；现代用法主要保留历史色彩。

senses.title: Strength shown in a fixed phrase
senses.definition: in the fixed phrases by virtue of and in virtue of, meaning because of or through
senses.definitionCN: 固定短语 by virtue of、in virtue of 中，意为凭借、由于
senses.example: She entered by virtue of her father's old pass.
senses.exampleCN: 她凭父亲旧日的通行证进去了。
senses.why: To act by virtue of something is to act on the strength given by it, so the old sense of power survives in this phrase.
senses.whyCN: by virtue of 某物行事，就是借它给的力量行事，旧有的「力量」义在这个短语里活了下来。

intro.en: Virtue comes from Latin virtus, strength or manliness, from vir, a man.
intro.cn: virtue 来自拉丁语 virtus（力量、男子气），源自 vir（男人）。

items.en: Vir meant a man, and virtus named the strength and courage expected of one.
items.cn: vir 意为男人，virtus 指男人应有的力量与勇气。

items.en: Cicero and others widened virtus to cover moral excellence of any kind.
items.cn: 西塞罗等人把 virtus 扩展到各种道德上的优秀。

items.en: Old French vertu carried the moral sense into English.
items.cn: 古法语 vertu 把道德义带进英语。

items.en: English added the sense of a good point in a thing and of the active power of a herb or stone.
items.cn: 英语又添上事物的长处，以及草药或石头的效力。

items.en: By virtue of keeps the older sense of power, and virtual grew beside it with a sense of what works in effect.
items.cn: by virtue of 保留了较旧的「力量」义，virtual 在旁边长出「实际起效」的意思。

note.en: The first group holds the same-root family, the second the words for goodness and for a good point.
note.cn: 第一组收同根词族，第二组收表示善与优点的词。

entries.definition: The plural of the noun.
An adjective meaning having or showing moral goodness.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有德行的、正直的」。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning acting in effect, though not in name or fact.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「实际起作用的、虚拟的」。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning almost, or in practice.
The quality of deserving praise, or a good point.
entries.definitionCN: 值得赞许之处，也指优点。

entries.definition: The general quality of being good.
The strengths of a case or a plan.
A bad habit or fault, the opposite of a virtue.

normalIntro.en: A word for manly strength became a word for moral strength, then for any useful strength.
normalIntro.cn: 一个表示男子之力的词，先变成道德之力，再变成任何可用的长处。

normal.en: Virtue comes from vir, a man, and virtus, the strength expected of him.
normal.cn: virtue 来自 vir（男人）与 virtus（他应有的力量）。

normal.en: By virtue of means because of, and keeps the old sense of power.
normal.cn: by virtue of 意为由于，保留着旧的「力量」义。

normal.en: Virtue is a good quality in a person; a virtue can also be a good point in a plan.
normal.cn: virtue 是人的好品质，也可指方案的长处。

normal.en: The plural is virtues; the adjective is virtuous.
normal.cn: 复数是 virtues，形容词是 virtuous。

normal.en: Vice is the opposite of virtue.
normal.cn: vice 是 virtue 的反面。

abstract.en: See a person standing straight with strength used for something good.
abstract.cn: 想象一人站得笔直，把力气用在正处。

abstract.en: Hear a teacher praising honesty instead of marks.
abstract.cn: 听老师不提分数，只夸诚实。

abstract.en: Feel the silent working power inside a bitter herb.
abstract.cn: 感受苦草根里那股无言的作用之力。

examples.en: Honesty is a virtue he never had to learn.
examples.cn: 诚实是他不必去学的一种美德。

examples.en: They chose the small hotel for the virtue of its quiet garden.
examples.cn: 他们选这家小旅馆，是因为它有安静花园这个优点。

examples.en: He was admitted by virtue of a special licence.
examples.cn: 他凭一张特别许可得以进入。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我求」——我求的是好品德，不是好分数。

root: 拉丁语 vir（男人）→ virtus（力量、勇气、美德）→ 古法语 vertu → 英语 virtue。

sensesIntro.en: Strength narrows to moral strength, then widens to a good point in a thing, to the power in a plant, and to a narrow historical sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 「力量」先缩成道德之力，再扩到事物的长处、植物的效力，以及一个狭窄的历史义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: strength held upright and used for good.
core.cn: 核心意象：站得笔直、用在正处的力量。

branches.en: The character branch: patience on the job.
branches.cn: 品格分支：工作所需的耐心。

branches.en: The good-point branch: a car that never breaks down.
branches.cn: 长处分支：从不坏的旧车。

branches.en: The power branch: a bitter root that works.
branches.cn: 效力分支：起作用的苦根。

branches.en: The historical branch: an old play about a woman's honour.
branches.cn: 历史分支：老戏里的名声。

branches.en: The phrase branch: entering by virtue of a pass.
branches.cn: 短语分支：凭通行证进入。

intro.en: Virt- comes from vir, a man; -ue arrived through French, and -ous, -ual, -ually build the family.
intro.cn: virt- 来自 vir（男人），-ue 经法语而来，-ous、-ual、-ually 撑起词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin vir and virtus are both recorded, and virtus is common in classical prose.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vir 与 virtus 均有记录，virtus 在古典散文里很常见。

items.example: The noun is the root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是词族的词根。

items.example: The noun first meant manly strength.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词最初指男子之力。

definition_zh: 设备；装备；器材
definition_en: the tools, machines, or gear needed for a particular purpose
core_image: 一堆工具整齐摆开，随时可以带上出发
scene: 登山前，队员检查了所有装备。 Before the climb, the team checked all their equipment.
sceneCN: 这里 equipment 是「装备」（第 1 个义项：为特定目的所需的工具和器材）；句意：登山前，队员检查了所有装备。

senses.title: Tools and machines for a purpose
senses.definition: the set of tools or machines used for a particular activity
senses.definitionCN: 用于某项活动的整套工具或机器
senses.example: The lab bought new equipment for the students.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室为学生购买了新设备。
senses.why: The noun adds -ment to equip, naming all the things supplied rather than the act of supplying.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词由 equip 加 -ment 构成，指被配备的全部物品，而不是配备的动作。

senses.title: Special gear for an activity
senses.definition: the clothing or gear needed for a sport, job, or journey
senses.definitionCN: 运动、工作或旅行所需的服装或装备
senses.example: Climbing equipment must be checked before every trip.
senses.exampleCN: 每次出行前都必须检查登山装备。
senses.why: Equipment can be personal gear as well as shared machines.
senses.whyCN: equipment 既可以是共用机器，也可以是个人装备。

senses.title: The act of fitting out
senses.definition: the process of supplying a person or place with what is needed, used in formal contexts
senses.definitionCN: 为某人或某地提供所需之物的过程，用于正式语境
senses.example: The equipment of the new hospital took a full year.
senses.exampleCN: 新医院的设备配置花了整整一年。
senses.why: The suffix -ment can name an action as well as its result, which keeps the older process sense alive.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ment 既可指动作也可指结果，因此保留了较老的「过程」含义。

intro.en: Equipment is equip plus -ment, from Old French esquiper, to fit out a ship.
intro.cn: equipment 是 equip 加 -ment，源自法语 esquiper（为船只配备物资）。

items.en: A Germanic skip word means ship.
items.cn: 日耳曼语中 skip 意为船。

items.en: Esquiper means to fit out a ship.
items.cn: esquiper 意为为船只配备。

items.en: Equip enters English as a verb.
items.cn: equip 作为动词进入英语。

items.en: The suffix -ment forms the noun equipment.
items.cn: 词尾 -ment 构成名词 equipment。

items.en: Equipment covers tools for work, sport, and medicine.
items.cn: 现代英语中，equipment 涵盖工作、运动和医疗器材。

note.en: Equipment is the noun of equip, close to its verb and adjective and to words for gear.
note.cn: equipment 是 equip 的名词，与它的动词、形容词形式以及表示「装备」的词相邻。

entries.definition: to supply with gear
having the needed gear
a set of equipment or a carriage
the equipment needed for an activity
a set of equipment for a purpose
goods needed for a task

normalIntro.en: Equipment is what equip supplies: the whole set of tools and gear.
normalIntro.cn: equipment 就是 equip 提供的东西：整套工具与装备。

normal.en: Equipment is uncountable, so say a piece of equipment.
normal.cn: equipment 不可数，所以说 a piece of equipment。

normal.en: Safety equipment protects workers.
normal.cn: safety equipment 保护工人。

normal.en: Medical equipment must be kept clean.
normal.cn: medical equipment 必须保持清洁。

normal.en: Heavy equipment moves earth and stone.
normal.cn: heavy equipment 用来移动土石。

normal.en: Compare gear: gear is more informal, equipment is broader and formal.
normal.cn: 对比 gear：gear 更口语，equipment 更宽泛正式。

abstract.en: Picture a neat row of tools laid out before a job.
abstract.cn: 想象干活前整齐摆开的一排工具。

abstract.en: Imagine a climber counting ropes and clips by a tent.
abstract.cn: 想象登山者在帐篷旁清点绳索和锁扣。

abstract.en: Think of a hospital room filled with humming machines.
abstract.cn: 想象一间充满机器低鸣的医院病房。

examples.en: All equipment must be stored in a dry room.
examples.cn: 所有设备都必须存放在干燥的房间里。

examples.en: She packed her camera equipment into two bags.
examples.cn: 她把摄影器材装进了两个包。

examples.en: The school spent a large sum on sports equipment.
examples.cn: 学校在体育器材上花了一大笔钱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「equip + ment」——被「配齐」的那些东西，就是设备；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 esquiper（为船只配备）→ 英语 equip（装备）＋ -ment → equipment，核心义「被配备起来的一整套用具」。

sensesIntro.en: Equipment first means the tools supplied, then personal gear, and in formal use the process of fitting out.
sensesIntro.cn: equipment 先指被提供的工具，再指个人装备，在正式用法中还指配置过程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a full set of tools laid out and ready.
core.cn: 核心意象：一整套工具摆放齐全待用。

branches.en: The tool set is the main modern sense.
branches.cn: 整套工具是现代主要义项。

branches.en: Personal gear is a narrower use.
branches.cn: 个人装备是较窄的用法。

branches.en: Fitting out keeps the older process sense.
branches.cn: 配置过程保留较老的过程含义。

branches.en: Both a lab machine and a climbing rope are supplied gear.
branches.cn: 实验室机器与登山绳都是被配备的装备。

branches.en: The equipment of a place is the result of equipping it.
branches.cn: 一个场所的设备是配置过程的结果。

intro.en: Equipment is equip with -ment, and it shares the fitting-out root with the verb.
intro.cn: equipment 是 equip 加 -ment，与动词共享「配备」词根。

latinIntro.en: Old French esquiper means to fit out a ship, probably from a Germanic ship word.
latinIntro.cn: 古法语 esquiper 意为为船只配备，可能来自日耳曼语表示船的单词。

items.example: Gear is the informal near word.

definition_zh: 政策；方针；原则；保险单；（古）治国术
definition_en: a course of action or set of principles adopted by a government or organization; a written contract of insurance
core_image: 一群人先定下走哪条路，再让所有人照这条路走
scene: 政府宣布了一项关于碳排放的新政策。 The government announced a new policy on carbon emissions.
sceneCN: 这里 policy 是「政府采取的行动方针」（第 1 个义项：政策）；句意：政府宣布了一项关于碳排放的新政策。场景要点：公共决定、成文、要被执行；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 明智的；精明的（同 polis 线，但词义已分化）

senses.title: A government's course of action
senses.titleCN: 政策：政府选定的那条路
senses.definition: a course of action chosen by a government or a political party on a matter of public concern
senses.definitionCN: 政府或政党在公共事务上选定的行动路线
senses.example: The government announced a new policy on carbon emissions.
senses.exampleCN: 政府宣布了一项关于碳排放的新政策。
senses.why: Greek politeia meant the conduct of public affairs. A policy is that conduct made explicit: a line the state decides to follow.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 politeia 意为“公共事务的治理”。policy 就是把这种治理摆到明处：国家决定要走的一条线。

senses.title: A rule adopted by an organization
senses.titleCN: 制度：组织内部定下的规矩
senses.definition: an agreed set of rules or principles that guides decisions inside a company, school, or other body
senses.definitionCN: 公司、学校或其他机构内部为决策而议定的一套规则或原则
senses.example: Company policy forbids personal use of the printers.
senses.exampleCN: 公司制度禁止把打印机用于私人用途。
senses.why: The state's line of action scaled down to any institution. What a body decides to keep doing becomes its standing policy.
senses.whyCN: 把国家的行动路线缩到任何机构。一个组织决定长期这么做，就成了它固定的制度。

senses.title: A written contract of insurance
senses.titleCN: 保险单：那张写满条款的纸
senses.definition: the written document in which an insurer agrees to cover specified risks for a premium
senses.definitionCN: 保险人同意以保费为代价承保特定风险的书面文件
senses.example: Read the policy carefully before you sign it.
senses.exampleCN: 签字之前要仔细读保险单。
senses.why: This is a different word in origin: Italian polizza meant a written note or proof. It came into English with the same spelling as the political word but from another root.
senses.whyCN: 这其实是另一个词源：意大利语 polizza 意为书面凭据或证明。它带着和政治义相同的拼写进入英语，但词根不同。

senses.title: Insurance cover in general
senses.definition: the protection bought under such a contract, spoken of as a thing one holds
senses.definitionCN: 依该合同获得的保障，被当作一件持有的东西来说
senses.example: The house is covered by a separate policy.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋房子另有一份保险。
senses.why: The paper stands for the protection it records. Holding the policy is holding the cover, so the word shifts from document to benefit.
senses.whyCN: 那张纸代表它所记录的保障。持有保单就是持有保障，于是词义从文件滑向利益。

senses.title: Archaic: statecraft
senses.definition: the art or practice of managing a state, in older usage
senses.definitionCN: 较古的用法，指治理国家的技艺或实践
senses.example: In Renaissance manuals, policy meant the craft of ruling well.
senses.exampleCN: 在文艺复兴时期的手册里，policy 指善于治国的技艺。
senses.why: This is the original sense from Greek politeia. It survives mainly in historical writing, where policy names the skill rather than one decision.
senses.whyCN: 这是来自希腊 politeia 的本义。它主要残存在历史叙述里，那里 policy 命名的是技能，而不是某一项决定。

senses.title: A party's declared programme
senses.definition: the set of positions and plans that a political party puts forward
senses.definitionCN: 一个政党提出的一套立场与计划
senses.example: The party's education policy won support in the cities.
senses.exampleCN: 该党的教育政策在城市赢得了支持。
senses.why: A party is a body that must state in advance what it will do. Its platform is policy in the form of a public promise.
senses.whyCN: 政党是一个必须事先说明将做什么的团体。它的政纲就是以公开承诺形式出现的政策。

senses.title: The field of public policy
senses.titleCN: 公共政策：研究怎么定的那门学问
senses.definition: the academic and professional study of how public decisions are made and evaluated
senses.definitionCN: 对公共决定如何作出与如何评估所作的学术与专业研究
senses.example: She studied public policy before joining the ministry.
senses.exampleCN: 她在进入部委之前学的是公共政策。
senses.why: Once policies are numerous and consequential, the making of them becomes an object of study, and the word names the field.
senses.whyCN: 当政策数量繁多且后果重大时，“制定政策”本身成了研究对象，这个词也就成了学科名。

senses.title: Expedient line of action
senses.definition: a line of action chosen for practical advantage rather than for principle
senses.definitionCN: 为实际好处而非为原则选择的行动路线
senses.example: He called it policy, though everyone knew it was a delay.
senses.exampleCN: 他称之为策略，但谁都知道那只是拖延。
senses.why: When principle is absent, the chosen line is still a line. The word then carries a hint of calculated convenience.
senses.whyCN: 没有原则时，所选的那条线仍是一条线。此时这个词就带上了“精于算计的便利”的暗示。

intro.en: Policy is two unrelated words that ended up spelled alike. One comes from the Greek word for city and gave us politics. The other comes from a Greek word for proof and gave us the insurance document.
intro.cn: policy 是两个本不相关的词，最后拼成了一样。一个来自希腊语表示“城邦”的词，也就是 politics 那一线；另一个来自希腊语表示“证明”的词，即保险单那一线。

items.en: Polis meant 'city, city-state'. It is the base of politics, police, polity, and metropolis. Its own earlier origin is uncertain.
items.cn: polis 意为“城、城邦”。它是 politics、police、polity、metropolis 的基底。它更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Politeia meant 'citizenship, the constitution, the conduct of public affairs'. It is polis plus the abstract noun ending -teia.
items.cn: politeia 意为“公民身份、政体、公共事务的治理”。它由 polis 加抽象名词词尾 -teia 构成。

items.en: Late Latin politia took the Greek word and used it for the ordering of a commonwealth. It is the direct parent of the political policy.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 politia 接取了这个希腊词，用来指共同体的秩序。它正是政治义 policy 的直接父辈。

items.en: Old French policie meant 'government, administration, political organization'. English borrowed it in the late 14th century, first as statecraft and then as a specific course of action.
items.cn: 古法语 policie 意为“政府、行政、政治组织”。英语于 14 世纪后期借入，先指治国术，后指具体的行动方针。

items.en: The insurance word has a separate chain: Greek apodeixis 'proof, demonstration' (apo- 'from' + deiknynai 'to show') became Medieval Latin apodissa, then Italian polizza 'a written note or certificate', then French police, and English policy in the 1560s. The identity with the political word is only in spelling.
items.cn: 保险义有另一条独立的链：希腊语 apodeixis“证明、演示”（apo-“出自”+ deiknynai“显示”）→ 中世纪拉丁 apodissa → 意大利语 polizza“书面凭据或证书” → 法语 police → 英语 16 世纪 60 年代的 policy。它与政治义只在拼写上相同。

items.en: The two words now share one spelling. Context decides: public policy, company policy, and insurance policy are three different things, and only the first two belong to the polis family.
items.cn: 两个词如今共用一种拼写。靠语境分辨：public policy、company policy、insurance policy 是三件不同的事，只有前两者属于 polis 词族。

note.en: The first group shares the Greek city root, including the French form that also produced the insurance sense. The second group collects words for rules and plans.
note.cn: 第一组共享希腊“城邦”词根，其中也含那个衍生出保险义的法语形式。第二组收表示规则与计划的词。

entries.definition: the activity of governing and competing for power. From Greek politikos 'of a citizen', from polis 'city'.
entries.definitionCN: 治理与争夺权力的活动。来自希腊语 politikos“公民的”，再往上为 polis“城邦”。

entries.definition: the body that enforces law. It goes back through French to Late Latin politia, the same polis family, but never means a policy.
entries.definitionCN: 执行法律的机构。它经法语回溯到晚期拉丁 politia，同属 polis 词族，但从不表示“政策”。

entries.definition: a politically organized society, or its form of government. It is the direct English descendant of Latin politia.
entries.definitionCN: 政治上有组织的社会，或其政体形式。它是拉丁 politia 的直接英语后裔。

entries.definition: the person who owns an insurance policy. It uses the insurance sense only.
entries.definitionCN: 持有保险单的人。它只使用保险义。

entries.definition: an overall plan for achieving a goal. Strategy is designed to win; policy is what an authority decides to follow.
entries.definitionCN: 为达成目标所作的总体计划。strategy 为取胜而设计；policy 是权威决定要遵循的路线。

entries.definition: a stated instruction about what may be done. A rule is one item; a policy is the principle behind a set of rules.
entries.definitionCN: 关于可以做什么的明文规定。rule 是单独一条；policy 是一组规则背后的原则。

entries.definition: advice about how to act, usually not compulsory. Guidelines are softer than policy, which is binding within an organization.
entries.definitionCN: 关于如何行动的指导意见，通常不强制。guideline 比 policy 软，后者在组织内具有约束力。

entries.definition: the fixed steps for doing something. Procedure is about how; policy is about what and why.
entries.definitionCN: 做某事的固定步骤。procedure 关乎怎么做；policy 关乎做什么和为什么。

entries.definition: a stated attitude toward an issue. A stance is where you stand; a policy is what you then do from there.
entries.definitionCN: 对某议题表明的态度。stance 是你站的位置；policy 是你从那里开始做的事。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks: the chosen road, the company handbook, the two word origins, the insurance paper, and the party platform.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手：选定的路、公司手册、两个词源、保险那张纸、政党纲领。

normal.en: A policy is a road picked in advance. Once picked, everyone walks it.
normal.cn: policy 是提前选好的路。一旦选定，所有人都走这条。

normal.en: Company policy is the page in the handbook that answers what you are allowed to do.
normal.cn: company policy 就是手册里那一页，回答“你能做什么”。

normal.en: Two roots, one spelling: polis gives public policy, apodeixis gives insurance policy.
normal.cn: 两个词根，一种拼写：polis 给出公共政策，apodeixis 给出保险单。

normal.en: An insurance policy is a paper you keep in a drawer until the day you need it.
normal.cn: 保险单是你放在抽屉里、直到需要那天才拿出来的那张纸。

normal.en: A party's policy is a promise written before the election so it can be checked after.
normal.cn: 政党政策是选前写下的承诺，好让选后被核对。

abstract.en: A policy is a decision made once and then applied many times; its power lies in not being re-argued every morning.
abstract.cn: 政策是一次作出、多次适用的决定；它的力量在于不必每天早上重新争论。

abstract.en: Every policy draws a line between what a group will consider and what it will ignore.
abstract.cn: 每一项政策都在“群体会考虑什么”与“群体将忽略什么”之间划一条线。

abstract.en: Rules are visible; the policy behind them is the invisible shape that makes the rules fit together.
abstract.cn: 规则是看得见的；规则背后的政策，是让这些规则彼此契合的无形形状。

examples.en: The Fed changed its interest-rate policy after inflation slowed.
examples.cn: 通胀放缓后，美联储改变了利率政策。

examples.en: Under company policy, all visitors must sign in at reception.
examples.cn: 按公司制度，所有来访者都必须在接待处登记。

examples.en: Her life insurance policy names her brother as the beneficiary.
examples.cn: 她的人寿保险单指定她弟弟为受益人。

dict_mnemonic.text: “破例色”要小心——政策（policy）一旦定下，就不能随便破例；不过保险单那一支跟这个谐音无关

root: 两支：①政治义：希腊 polis“城邦”→ politeia“公共治理”→ 拉丁 politia → 古法语 policie → 英语 policy（14 世纪末）；②保险义：希腊 apodeixis“证明”→ 中世纪拉丁 apodissa → 意大利 polizza → 法语 police → 英语 policy（1560s）。

sensesIntro.en: The political senses all describe a line an authority decides to follow, from a state's grand course down to one office's rules. The insurance senses came from a different Greek word and only borrowed the spelling.
sensesIntro.cn: 政治义的各个义项都描述权威决定要遵循的一条线，从国家的大政到单个办公室的规矩。保险义来自另一个希腊词，只借用了拼写。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a group agreeing on one road before anyone starts walking.
core.cn: 核心意象：一群人在动身之前先议定只走一条路。

branches.en: PUBLIC LINE: what a government or party decides to do.
branches.cn: 公共路线：政府或政党决定要做的事。

branches.en: INSTITUTION: rules inside a body, and the study of how such decisions are made.
branches.cn: 机构：团体内部的规则，以及研究这类决定如何作出的学问。

branches.en: CRAFT: the older sense, governing as a skill rather than as one decision.
branches.cn: 技艺：较古的义项，把治理看成技能而非某一项决定。

branches.en: EXPEDIENCY: a line chosen for advantage, which is policy without principle.
branches.cn: 权宜：为利益选择的路线，即没有原则的政策。

branches.en: INSURANCE: a separate word, the document and the cover it represents.
branches.cn: 保险：另一个词，指文件以及它所代表的保障。

intro.en: The political family is built on the Greek word for city. The insurance word belongs to a completely different set of pieces, which is why mixing them is a common error.
intro.cn: 政治义词族建立在希腊语“城邦”一词上。保险义属于完全不同的一套构件，所以把两者混为一谈是常见错误。

latinIntro.en: Latin politia carried the city root into French and English; apodissa carried the proof root into Italian and then French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 politia 把“城邦”词根带进法语和英语；apodissa 则把“证明”词根带进意大利语，再进法语。

items.meaningCN: 表示学科或活动的后缀

items.exampleCN: 证明（保险义的最早源头）

items.meaningCN: 表示过程或动作的名词后缀
表示状态、团体或活动的名词后缀

definition_zh: 失业；失业状态；失业率；失业人数
definition_en: the state of not having a paid job, or the number or rate of people in that state
core_image: 就业大门前一条越排越长的队伍
scene: 经济下行时，就业中心门口的队伍从街角排到了邮局。 Unemployment rose sharply in the region last winter.
sceneCN: 这里 unemployment 是名词「失业；失业率」（第 1 个义项：无工作的状态）；句意为去年冬天该地区失业率急剧上升。

pos.zh: 失业率；失业人数（统计义）

derivatives.zh: 由名词 -ment 换为形容词分词 -ed 构成，义为「失业的」
去掉否定前缀后的词基名词，义为「就业；雇用」
词基动词，义为「雇用；使用」

senses.title: The state of having no job
senses.definition: the condition of not having a paid job while being available for work
senses.definitionCN: 没有有薪工作但可参加工作的一种状态
senses.example: Two years of unemployment taught him to budget carefully.
senses.exampleCN: 两年的失业生活教会了他精打细算。
senses.why: The suffix -ment turns the negative participle into a thing: the absence of employment becomes a state you can be inside.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ment 把否定分词变成一件「东西」：雇用的缺席成了一种人可以身处其中的状态。

senses.title: The number of people without work
senses.definition: the total count of people who are without work, as a statistic
senses.definitionCN: 没有工作的人的总数，作为一项统计数字
senses.example: Unemployment fell by ten thousand this quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 本季度失业人数减少了一万。
senses.why: A state can be counted by counting the people in it; the word slides from condition to headcount.
senses.whyCN: 状态可以通过清点其中的人数来计量；这个词便从「状况」滑向「人数」。

senses.title: The unemployment rate
senses.definition: the percentage of the labour force without work, as in the unemployment rate
senses.definitionCN: 劳动力中无工作者的百分比，如失业率
senses.example: The unemployment rate inched up to six point two percent.
senses.exampleCN: 失业率微升至百分之六点二。
senses.why: Economists prefer ratios to headcounts; the same word now names the measure as well as the state.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家偏好比率而非绝对人数；同一个词于是又承担了「度量」之义。

senses.title: Idleness of resources
senses.definition: the state of land, capital, or machines not being used
senses.definitionCN: 土地、资金或机器未被使用的状态
senses.example: The report also measured unemployment of farmland in the district.
senses.exampleCN: 该报告还统计了区内农田的闲置情况。
senses.why: Since employ means to use, unemployment can name any unused thing, not only unused people.
senses.whyCN: 既然 employ 本义是「使用」，unemployment 就可指任何未被使用之物，而不只是未被雇用的人。

senses.title: Long-term joblessness
senses.definition: prolonged joblessness lasting months or years, as in long-term unemployment
senses.definitionCN: 持续数月或数年的长期无工作状态，如长期失业
senses.example: Long-term unemployment erodes both skills and confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 长期失业会消磨技能，也会消磨信心。
senses.why: A temporary gap hardens into a condition; the noun carries the weight of time spent outside work.
senses.whyCN: 暂时的空缺会硬化为一种处境；这个名词承载着工作之外流逝的时间之重。

senses.title: Seasonal joblessness
senses.definition: joblessness caused by the seasons of a trade, as in seasonal unemployment
senses.definitionCN: 由行业季节引起的失业，如季节性失业
senses.example: Seasonal unemployment peaks in the quiet winter months.
senses.exampleCN: 季节性失业在淡季的冬季达到高峰。
senses.why: Work has tides; the word marks the low water that returns with the calendar.
senses.whyCN: 工作有潮汐；这个词标记着随日历周期性回落的低水位。

senses.title: Structural joblessness
senses.definition: joblessness caused by changes in an economy rather than a downturn, as in structural unemployment
senses.definitionCN: 由经济结构变化而非经济衰退引起的失业，如结构性失业
senses.example: Automation created structural unemployment in the coalfields.
senses.exampleCN: 自动化在煤田地区造成了结构性失业。
senses.why: When the jobs themselves vanish rather than the demand, the absence is built into the structure of work.
senses.whyCN: 当消失的是岗位本身而非需求时，「缺席」便被建造进了工作结构之中。

senses.title: A social and political problem
senses.definition: joblessness treated as a public issue to be fought or reduced, as in fighting unemployment
senses.definitionCN: 被视为需治理或降低的公共问题的失业，如「治理失业」
senses.example: The government promised to fight unemployment with new training schemes.
senses.exampleCN: 政府承诺以新的培训计划来治理失业。
senses.why: Once counted, a state becomes an enemy: societies name the problem so they can act on it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦被计量，状态便成了敌人：社会给问题命名，是为了能够对它采取行动。

intro.en: Unemployment stacks three layers: a Latin root, a French verb, and an Old English negative prefix.
intro.cn: unemployment 叠了三层：拉丁词根、法语动词、古英语否定前缀。

items.en: Latin implicare meant to enfold or entangle; its participle gave the sense of being held or busy.
items.cn: 拉丁语 implicare 意为「包住；缠住」，其分词形式衍生出「被占用；忙碌」之义。

items.en: Old French employer meant to use, apply, or engage.
items.cn: 古法语 employer 意为「使用；应用；聘用」。

items.en: The verb entered English in the fifteenth century; employment followed as its noun.
items.cn: 动词于十五世纪进入英语，其名词 employment 随之出现。

items.en: The negative prefix un- is native Old English, cognate with Latin in- and Greek a(n)-.
items.cn: 否定前缀 un- 是古英语本族成分，与拉丁语 in-、希腊语 a(n)- 同源。

items.en: The noun unemployment is recorded from the late nineteenth century, when labour statistics demanded an abstract term.
items.cn: 名词 unemployment 约自十九世纪末有记录，当时劳动统计需要这样一个抽象名词。

items.en: Today unemployment is an economic indicator as much as a personal condition.
items.cn: 如今 unemployment 既是个人处境，也是一项经济指标。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the employ family and un- counterparts; the near-meaning group gathers nouns for joblessness and idleness.
note.cn: 形近组收 employ 词族与 un- 对应词；近义组收失业与闲置类名词。

entries.definition: The adjective for a person in this state.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指处于失业状态的人。

entries.definition: The positive noun: having work or hiring people.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「就业；雇用」，为本词的正面形式。

entries.definition: The base verb: to use or to hire.
entries.definitionCN: 词基动词，义为「使用；雇用」。

entries.definition: The American term for payments to the jobless.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，美式说法，指付给失业者的救济金。

entries.definition: Putting forces or systems into position; shares the -ment ending but not the Latin root, only similar in sound.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「部署」，与 unemployment 词根无关只是拼写相近，词源无关。

entries.definition: The state of having no job; plainer and more direct.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「无工作状态」，措辞更朴素直接。

entries.definition: The state of not working; broader, covering machines and time.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「闲置；空闲」，适用面更广，也指机器与时间。

entries.definition: The British term for losing a job because the post is cut.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，英式用语，指因岗位撤销而被裁员。

entries.definition: The act of ending employment for economic reasons.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「裁员；暂时解雇」，强调经济原因。

entries.definition: Periods when machines or systems are not working.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「停机时间」，指机器或系统停止运转的时段。

normalIntro.en: Five anchors from the layered structure of the word.
normalIntro.cn: 五个来自词语分层结构的记忆锚点。

normal.en: Un- + employ + -ment: not + use/hire + state.
normal.cn: un- 加 employ 加 -ment：不 + 使用/雇用 + 状态。

normal.en: Employment is the door; unemployment is standing outside it.
normal.cn: employment 是那扇门，unemployment 是站在门外。

normal.en: Unemployed describes the person; unemployment describes the state or the number.
normal.cn: unemployed 形容人，unemployment 形容状态或数字。

normal.en: Employ is one syllable shorter than employee and employer.
normal.cn: employ 比 employee、employer 都短一个音节，是词族的根。

normal.en: The -ment family: employment, unemployment, entertainment, government.
normal.cn: -ment 词族：employment、unemployment、entertainment、government。

abstract.en: Picture a queue outside an employment office growing longer each winter.
abstract.cn: 想象就业中心门外的队伍，每个冬天都在变长。

abstract.en: Un- flips the sign on the board: hiring becomes not hiring.
abstract.cn: un- 翻转了公告牌上的符号：「招聘」变成了「不招聘」。

abstract.en: A rate is the queue made into a number on a chart.
abstract.cn: 「率」就是那条队伍变成图表上的一个数字。

examples.en: Unemployment among young workers has doubled in five years.
examples.cn: 五年来青年工人的失业人数翻了一番。

examples.en: She received unemployment benefits while retraining as a nurse.
examples.cn: 她在接受护士再培训期间领取失业救济金。

examples.en: The scheme aims to cut unemployment in the former mining towns.
examples.cn: 该计划旨在降低前矿业城镇的失业率。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安·因普洛伊门特」——安（un 不）因普洛伊（employ 雇用）的门（ment）关上了：失业这道门

root: unemployment 由古英语否定前缀 un- 加 employment 构成；employment 经古法语 employer「使用；聘用」溯至拉丁语 implicare「包住；缠住」（分词形式衍生「被占用」之义）；un- 与拉丁语 in-、希腊语 a(n)- 同源；名词形式在十九世纪末随劳动统计制度兴起而定型。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses of unemployment move from a personal condition outward: one person's empty hands become a headcount, a rate, a tide, a structure, and finally a problem a whole society must fight.
sensesIntro.cn: unemployment 的八个义项由个人处境向外扩展：一个人空着的双手，变成人数、比率、潮汐、结构，最终成为全社会必须应对的问题。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a queue outside the employment office door
core.cn: 核心意象：就业中心门外排起的队伍

branches.en: THE STATE: joblessness as a condition, short or long.
branches.cn: 状态线：作为处境的失业，或短或长。

branches.en: THE NUMBER: headcounts and rates on the economist's chart.
branches.cn: 数字线：经济学家图表上的人数与比率。

branches.en: THE THINGS: land, capital and machines left unused.
branches.cn: 器物线：未被使用的土地、资金与机器。

branches.en: THE TIDES: seasonal lows and structural shifts in work.
branches.cn: 潮汐线：工作的季节性低谷与结构性变动。

branches.en: THE FIGHT: joblessness named as a problem societies act on.
branches.cn: 治理线：被命名为公共问题的失业。

intro.en: Unemployment is a three-layer construction: native prefix, French verb, Latin root.
intro.cn: unemployment 是三层结构：本族前缀、法语动词、拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: The deep root is Latin implicare; its family shows the fold-and-use shift.
latinIntro.cn: 深层词根是拉丁语 implicare；其词族展示了「缠绕→使用」的语义转移。

items.example: It forms implicate with the Latin root.
items.exampleCN: 它与拉丁词根构成 implicate。

latinEntries.example: The ancestor of employ and imply.
latinEntries.exampleCN: employ 与 imply 的祖先。

latinEntries.example: It forms apply via Old French aplier.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 经由古法语 aplier 构成 apply。

derivatives.zh: 由名词 -ment 换为形容词分词 -ed 构成，义为「失业的」
去掉否定前缀后的词基名词，义为「就业；雇用」
词基动词，义为「雇用；使用」

definition_zh: 蘑菇；菌类；迅速增长；迅速涌现
definition_en: a fungus that grows above ground with a soft stem and a cap, many kinds of which are eaten; also to grow, spread or appear very quickly
core_image: 雨后草地上几朵圆伞般的白菇一夜之间撑开，挤满了整片泥地
scene: 清晨的草地还带着露水，几朵白伞样的菌子从落叶堆里顶出来，比前一天大了整整一圈。 Mushrooms appeared across the lawn after two days of rain.
sceneCN: 这里是「蘑菇、菌类」（第 1 个义项：有菌盖与菌柄的肉质真菌）；句意为连下两天雨后，草坪上冒出了一片蘑菇。图中可辨识物件：露水、落叶堆、白色菌盖。

derivatives.zh: 由 mushroom 加 -ing 构成，义为「迅速增多；采蘑菇」
由 mushroom 加表示「人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「采蘑菇的人」

senses.title: A fleshy fungus with a stem and a cap
senses.definition: a fungus that grows above ground with a soft stem and a cap, many kinds of which are eaten
senses.definitionCN: 长在地面、有柔软菌柄与菌盖的真菌，其中许多种类可食用
senses.example: She sliced the mushrooms and added them to the pan.
senses.exampleCN: 她把蘑菇切片放进锅里。
senses.why: The English name probably comes from French mousseron, a word for a kind of mushroom, later reshaped by association with moss where the fungi grow.
senses.whyCN: 英语这个词很可能来自法语 mousseron（一种蘑菇），后来又因为菌子多生于苔藓而被改写成形。

senses.title: Fungi as a group in ordinary use
senses.definition: the group of such fungi, especially the edible kinds sold or gathered as food
senses.definitionCN: 这类真菌的整体，尤指市场上出售或采来食用的种类
senses.example: Wild mushrooms are best kept apart from the rest of the shopping.
senses.exampleCN: 野生蘑菇最好和其余买来的东西分开放。
senses.why: Because cooks and foragers deal with many kinds at once, the same word came to name the category in the kitchen rather than one species.
senses.whyCN: 厨师和采菌人一次面对许多种类，于是同一个词在厨房里成了对整个类别的称呼，而不是某一个物种。

senses.title: To increase very fast
senses.definition: to grow, spread or appear very quickly, like fungi rising overnight
senses.definitionCN: 像菌子一夜冒出那样，迅速地增长、扩散或出现
senses.example: Sales mushroomed after the advertisement ran.
senses.exampleCN: 广告播出之后，销量迅速增长。
senses.why: The picture of a fungus swelling up in a single night supplied a ready metaphor for anything that multiplies suddenly.
senses.whyCN: 菌子在夜里一下子撑开的画面，为任何骤然增多的事物提供了现成的比喻。

intro.en: The name of the mushroom is one of the less certain words in English: it is probably French in origin and was later reshaped by English speakers.
intro.cn: 蘑菇这个词的来源在英语里算不上确定：一般认为出自法语，后来被英语使用者改了形状。

items.en: The earliest forms are hard to trace, and dictionaries mark the origin as uncertain rather than settled.
items.cn: 最早的词形难以追溯，词典把来源标为不确定，而不是已有定论。

items.en: A likely source is French mousseron, a name for a kind of mushroom, which English borrowed and altered.
items.cn: 一般认为来源是法语 mousseron，一种蘑菇的名称，英语借入后改动了拼写。

items.en: English speakers seem to have reshaped the word so that it echoed moss, the damp ground where fungi appear.
items.cn: 英语使用者似乎把这个词改得像 moss（苔藓），也就是菌子常出现的潮湿地表。

items.en: By the sixteenth century mushroom and mushrump were both in use for the edible fungus.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，mushroom 与 mushrump 两种写法都用来指可食用的菌类。

items.en: Modern English fixed the spelling and, from the nineteenth century, extended the word to anything growing with sudden speed.
items.cn: 现代英语固定了拼写，并从十九世纪起把词义扩展到任何迅速增长的事物。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that merely share the shape of mushroom; the near-meaning group collects fungi, their parts and their relatives.
note.cn: 形近组收只是与 mushroom 字形相近的词；近义组收真菌、真菌的构造以及相关词。

entries.definition: Soft, wet pulp, or a command to a team of dogs; only the opening shape resembles this word.
entries.definitionCN: 柔软湿糊的东西，或对拉雪橇犬发出的口令；只是开头形似。

entries.definition: Soft and wet, or excessively sentimental; the shape is close but the word comes from mash.
entries.definitionCN: 又软又湿的，或过分伤感的；字形相近，但这个词来自 mash。

entries.definition: A small green plant that carpets damp ground; it may have influenced the shape of this word, yet it is a different word.
entries.definitionCN: 铺在潮湿地表的小型绿色植物；它可能影响过这个词的写法，但本身是另一个词。

entries.definition: Low wet ground; the spelling and sound are close, the meaning is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 低洼潮湿之地；拼写与读音相近，意义无关。

entries.definition: Any member of the group that includes moulds, yeasts and mushrooms.
entries.definitionCN: 包括霉菌、酵母与蘑菇在内的一类生物。

entries.definition: An umbrella-shaped fungus, especially a poisonous one.
entries.definitionCN: 伞状真菌，尤指有毒的那种。

entries.definition: The reproductive cell of fungi and other simple organisms.
entries.definitionCN: 真菌等简单生物的繁殖细胞。

entries.definition: A soft fungal growth on damp or decaying matter.
entries.definitionCN: 潮湿物或腐败物上长出的真菌。

normalIntro.en: The origin is uncertain, the spelling echoes moss, and the sudden swelling of a fungus gave English a verb for rapid growth.
normalIntro.cn: 来源不确定，拼写又与苔藓相近，而菌子骤然撑开的画面，给英语提供了一个表示迅速增长的动词。

normal.en: The likely French source mousseron already named a mushroom, so the word arrived with its meaning attached.
normal.cn: 一般认为的法语来源 mousseron 本来就指一种蘑菇，所以这个词是带着意思进来的。

normal.en: The modern spelling echoes moss, and mushrooms do rise from damp mossy ground, which makes the link easy to remember even if it is not the true source.
normal.cn: 现代拼写与 moss（苔藓）相近，蘑菇又真从潮湿的苔藓地里冒出来，所以这层联系即使不是真来源也很好记。

normal.en: Mushroom is both noun and verb, so one shape covers the food and the sudden swelling of numbers.
normal.cn: mushroom 既是名词又是动词，一个形状同时管食物和数量的骤增。

normal.en: The plural mushrooms is usual in the kitchen, while the verb takes mushroomed and mushrooming.
normal.cn: 厨房里常用复数 mushrooms，而动词则取 mushroomed 与 mushrooming。

normal.en: Mushroom cloud borrows the cap shape for the plume of an explosion, showing how far the picture travels.
normal.cn: mushroom cloud 借菌盖的形状来形容爆炸的烟柱，可见这个画面能走多远。

abstract.en: Picture white caps pushing through wet leaves overnight, each one a small umbrella.
abstract.cn: 想象一夜之间，白色菌盖顶开湿叶，每一朵都是一把小伞。

abstract.en: A fungus appears without being planted, which is why the word can mean anything that springs up unplanned.
abstract.cn: 菌子没人种也会出现，所以这个词可以指任何不请自来的东西。

abstract.en: The same shape that feeds people also lends its name to explosions, so mushroom carries both growth and blast.
abstract.cn: 同一个形状既养育人，也给爆炸命名，所以 mushroom 同时带着生长与爆裂。

examples.en: He added mushrooms and cream to the soup.
examples.cn: 他往汤里加了蘑菇和奶油。

examples.en: The small business mushroomed into a chain within three years.
examples.cn: 这家小生意三年之内迅速扩张成了连锁店。

examples.en: Some mushrooms in the wood are poisonous and should not be picked.
examples.cn: 林子里有些蘑菇有毒，不该采。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马什鲁姆」——雨后草地一夜撑开一片小伞；记住 mushroom 是蘑菇。

root: 一般认为源自法语 mousseron（一种蘑菇），英语借入后改写，可能受 moss（苔藓）影响；确切来源不确定，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a cap rising from damp ground; the senses divide into the edible fungus, the group of fungi, and sudden rapid growth.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是从潮湿地表顶出的菌盖；义项分出可食用的菌子、菌类整体，以及突然的迅速增长。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: white caps pushing through wet leaves overnight, each one a small umbrella.
core.cn: 核心意象：一夜之间，白色菌盖顶开湿叶，每一朵都是一把小伞。

branches.en: white caps pushing through wet leaves
branches.cn: 湿叶间顶出的白色菌盖

branches.en: a basket holding several kinds of fungi
branches.cn: 装着几种菌子的一只篮子

branches.en: a chart line rising almost straight up
branches.cn: 几乎笔直上升的曲线

branches.en: a crowd forming at a door in minutes
branches.cn: 几分钟内就在门口聚起的人群

branches.en: one shape that feeds a family and also names a blast
branches.cn: 既喂饱一家人、又给爆炸命名的同一个形状

intro.en: A probable French source, a reshaped ending and two English compounds and suffixes carry this uncertain but vivid word.
intro.cn: 一个很可能的法语来源、一个被改写的词尾，以及几个英语复合形式与后缀，撑起了这个来源不确定却画面鲜明的词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded: mushroom is probably of French origin, and the word has no settled Latin relative.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录：mushroom 一般认为出自法语，并没有确定的拉丁亲属词。

items.meaningCN: 来源不确定的改写词尾

items.meaning: cloud shaped like a cap after an explosion

definition_zh: 间隔；间歇；幕间休息
definition_en: a period of time between two events, or a space between two things
core_image: 两根柱子之间空出一段距离，阳光正好落在中间那块地面上
scene: 公交车每隔十分钟来一辆，站台上的人看着时刻表估摸下一班。 There was a long interval before the doctor came out.
sceneCN: 这里 interval 是「间隔」（第 1 个义项：两个事件之间的时间段），句意为过了很久医生才出来。画面里的物件：时刻表、站台长椅、手表。

pos.zh: 名词：间隔；间歇；幕间休息

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ic 构成，义为「间隔的；音程的」
结构相近的近亲，义为「幕间插曲」

senses.title: Time between events
senses.definition: the length of time separating two events or points
senses.definitionCN: 把两个事件或两个时点隔开的那段时间
senses.example: Buses run here at intervals of fifteen minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的公交车每十五分钟一班。
senses.why: Latin intervallum meant the space between rampart walls.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 intervallum 本指城墙之间的空地。

senses.title: Space between things
senses.definition: the distance or empty space between two objects placed apart
senses.definitionCN: 两件分开放置之物之间的距离或空隙
senses.example: Plant the young trees at wide intervals.
senses.exampleCN: 树苗要按较宽的间距栽种。
senses.why: The word began with space, so this sense is the older picture returning.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本来讲空间，所以这一义项是更古老的画面回来了。

senses.title: A break in a show
senses.definition: a pause between the parts of a performance, when the audience may leave their seats
senses.definitionCN: 演出各部分之间的暂停，观众可以离座
senses.example: We talked about the play during the interval.
senses.exampleCN: 中场休息时我们聊了聊这部戏。
senses.why: A theatre simply uses the time sense for its own calendar of acts.
senses.whyCN: 剧院只是把时间义用在自己分幕的日程上。

senses.title: A gap in pitch
senses.definition: the distance in pitch between two musical notes
senses.definitionCN: 两个音之间在音高上的距离
senses.example: A fifth is the easiest interval to hear.
senses.exampleCN: 五度是最容易听出来的音程。
senses.why: Music measures distance too, so the space word works between notes.
senses.whyCN: 音乐也丈量距离，于是空间词也能用在音符之间。

intro.en: Interval comes from Latin intervallum, the space between two palisades of a camp.
intro.cn: interval 来自拉丁语 intervallum，指军营两道栅栏之间的空地。

items.en: Vallum was the wall of stakes round a camp.
items.cn: vallum 是营寨四周的木桩墙。

items.en: Intervallum was the open space left between walls.
items.cn: intervallum 是两道墙之间留出的空地。

items.en: The word also measured gaps in time and in speech.
items.cn: 这个词也用来量时间与话语中的空档。

items.en: French intervalle carried the spacing sense to English.
items.cn: 法语 intervalle 把「间距」义带入英语。

items.en: Theatres and musicians gave the word its break and pitch senses.
items.cn: 剧院与音乐家又给它添上休息与音程义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the inter- prefix; the near-meaning group holds words for gaps.
note.cn: 形近组共用 inter- 前缀；近义组收表示空档的词。

entries.definition: Situated inside something.
Necessary as part of a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「不可缺少的」，拼写相近。

entries.definition: A short piece played between acts.
An empty space or a missing part.
A short stop before carrying on.
A rest between periods of activity.

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the picture of two posts with a measured gap between them.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子守着「两根柱子之间量出一段空档」的画面。

normal.en: inter- between plus vallum wall gives the space between walls.
normal.cn: inter-「之间」加 vallum「墙」就是两墙之间的空地。

normal.en: At regular intervals is the phrase of clocks and buses.
normal.cn: at regular intervals 是钟表和公交的说法。

normal.en: The interval in a play is exactly a gap in the action.
normal.cn: 戏里的 interval 正是情节中间的空档。

normal.en: Musicians count the interval between two notes.
normal.cn: 音乐家数两个音之间的音程。

normal.en: Interval, not Internet: the middle letters are -erv- not -ernet-.
normal.cn: 是 interval 不是 internet：中间是 -erv- 而非 -ernet-。

abstract.en: An interval is silence given a length.
abstract.cn: 间隔就是被量出长度的沉默。

abstract.en: Two notes need the empty air between them to become music.
abstract.cn: 两个音要有中间的空处才成为音乐。

abstract.en: Life is measured in intervals as much as in events.
abstract.cn: 人生不只由事件计量，也由事件之间的间隔计量。

examples.en: The nurse checked his pulse at short intervals.
examples.cn: 护士每隔一小会儿就看一次他的脉搏。

examples.en: There is a wide interval between their two houses.
examples.cn: 他们两家的房子之间隔着很大的距离。

examples.en: During the interval the orchestra stayed on stage.
examples.cn: 幕间休息时乐队留在台上。

dict_mnemonic.text: inter（之间）+ val（墙）——两墙之间空出来的那段

root: 拉丁语 vallum「木桩墙」→ intervallum「两墙之间的空地」→ 古法语 intervalle → 英语 interval。同族有 intervallic、interlude。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: time between events, space between objects, a break in a show, and pitch distance in music.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：事件之间的时间、物体之间的空间、演出中间的休息，以及音乐中的音程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two posts, and the measured empty ground between them.
core.cn: 核心意象：两根柱子，中间量出的一段空地。

branches.en: THE TICKET: the wait before the next bus.
branches.cn: 车票这条线：下一班车之前的等待。

branches.en: THE FIELD: the distance planted between two trees.
branches.cn: 田地这条线：两棵树之间留出的距离。

branches.en: THE CURTAIN: the pause between two acts.
branches.cn: 幕布这条线：两幕之间的暂停。

branches.en: THE SOUND: the gap that makes two notes a melody.
branches.cn: 声音这条线：让两个音成曲的距离。

branches.en: THE LINK: the same gap, read on a clock or on the ground.
branches.cn: 连接线：同一个空档，或读作时间或读作地面。

intro.en: Interval is inter- "between" plus Latin vallum "rampart", with the noun ending lost in French.
intro.cn: interval 是 inter-「之间」加拉丁语 vallum「壁垒」，名词词尾在法语中磨掉了。

latinIntro.en: Latin vallum and intervallum are recorded; the root also gives English wall.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vallum 与 intervallum 均有记载，这个词根也给英语带来 wall。

items.example: It marks the space of two sides.
items.exampleCN: 它标出两侧之间的空处。

items.example: The root survives in English wall.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根在英语 wall 中留存。

items.example: The noun named the camp wall.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指营寨的围墙。

items.example: The noun is the direct source.

items.meaning: a side of a building or fort
items.example: It keeps the old root alive.
Another inter- word of the same pattern.
items.exampleCN: 同一模式的另一个 inter- 词。

definition_zh: 平的；公寓；平淡的；瘪了的
definition_en: having an even surface, an apartment, dull without energy, or deflated
core_image: 一块刚擀开的桌面，摸不到一点起伏
scene: 我们在一间小小的公寓里住了两晚。 We stayed two nights in a small flat.
sceneCN: 这里 flat 是「公寓」（第 2 个义项）；句意：我们在一间小小的公寓里住了两晚。

senses.title: Level
senses.definition: having a surface without slopes or bumps
senses.definitionCN: 表面没有倾斜或凸起的
senses.example: The land is flat for miles.
senses.exampleCN: 这片土地平坦绵延数英里。
senses.why: This is the literal physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最字面的物理义项。

senses.title: Apartment
senses.definition: a set of rooms for living on one floor
senses.definitionCN: 位于同一层的一套住所
senses.example: We stayed two nights in a small flat.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在一间小公寓里住了两晚。
senses.why: A flat is one level of a building, hence a dwelling.
senses.whyCN: 公寓占楼的一层，因此用「平」来表示。

senses.title: Dull
senses.definition: lacking interest, energy, or variation
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏趣味、活力或变化的
senses.example: The party felt flat after the speeches.
senses.exampleCN: 讲话结束后聚会变得平淡。
senses.why: Something without peaks seems level and lifeless.
senses.whyCN: 没有起伏的东西显得平坦而无生气。

senses.title: Deflated
senses.definition: having lost air, as a tyre
senses.definitionCN: 像轮胎一样失去空气的
senses.example: The tyre went flat on the way home.
senses.exampleCN: 回家路上轮胎瘪了。
senses.why: A deflated tyre is pressed flat to the ground.
senses.whyCN: 瘪胎被压平贴在地面上。

intro.en: Flat comes from Old Norse flatr, related to Old English flet, a floor or dwelling.
intro.cn: flat 源自古诺尔斯语 flatr，与古英语 flet（地板、住所）相关。

items.en: Flatr meant level or spread out.
items.cn: flatr 意为平坦的、铺开的。

items.en: Flat named a level surface.
items.cn: flat 指平坦的表面。

items.en: A flat became a dwelling on one floor.
items.cn: flat 开始指一层的住所。

items.en: The word described dull or lifeless things.
items.cn: 这个词用来形容平淡无生气的事物。

items.en: A flat tyre meant one emptied of air.
items.cn: flat tyre 指被放空空气的轮胎。

note.en: Flat is compared with similar-looking words and with words for level surfaces.
note.cn: 把 flat 与形近词以及表示平整表面的词作比较。

entries.definition: a piece that moves loosely
a baked custard dish
heavy criticism or gunfire
having an even surface
level and smooth
having no bumps

normalIntro.en: Flat is one even plane: land, a floor to live on, a mood without peaks, a tyre without air.
normalIntro.cn: flat 就是一个平面：土地、居住的一层、没有起伏的情绪、没有气的轮胎。

normal.en: The road is flat and straight.
normal.cn: 这条路平坦笔直。

normal.en: They rent a flat in town.
normal.cn: 他们在城里租了一套公寓。

normal.en: The joke fell flat.
normal.cn: 那个笑话没逗笑人。

normal.en: We changed the flat tyre.
normal.cn: 我们换了瘪掉的轮胎。

normal.en: Flatten the dough with a roller.
normal.cn: 用擀面杖把面团擀平。

abstract.en: A flat surface hides how much ground it covers.
abstract.cn: 平坦的表面看不出它覆盖了多远。

abstract.en: Without hills, a landscape has no surprises.
abstract.cn: 没有山丘，风景就少了惊喜。

abstract.en: Even a flat road still leads somewhere.
abstract.cn: 即使平坦的路也通向某处。

examples.en: We stayed two nights in a small flat.
examples.cn: 我们在一间小公寓里住了两晚。

examples.en: The land is flat for miles.
examples.cn: 这片土地平坦绵延数英里。

examples.en: The tyre went flat on the way home.
examples.cn: 回家路上轮胎瘪了。

dict_mnemonic.text: flat 源自古诺尔斯语 flatr（平坦），核心义「平」，由平的地面引申为一层公寓、平淡与瘪掉。

root: 源自古诺尔斯语 flatr（平坦、铺开），核心义「没有起伏的平面」。

sensesIntro.en: Flat means level, an apartment, dull, or emptied of air.
sensesIntro.cn: flat 意为平坦的、公寓、平淡的或瘪了的。

core.en: A surface with no height or dip.
core.cn: 没有高低起伏的表面。

branches.en: Ground without slopes or bumps.
branches.cn: 没有坡度和凸起的地面。

branches.en: One level of a building to live on.
branches.cn: 楼里供居住的一层。

branches.en: A mood or event without peaks.
branches.cn: 没有起伏的情绪或事件。

branches.en: A tyre pressed flat by lost air.
branches.cn: 因漏气被压平的轮胎。

branches.en: The level surface and the dwelling share one word.
branches.cn: 平面与住宅共用一个词。

intro.en: Flat is a Germanic word that builds words for pressing, manner, and shared homes.
intro.cn: flat 是日耳曼语词，能构成表示压平、方式和合住的词。

latinIntro.en: Flat has no Latin ancestor; Latin planus, level, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: flat 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 planus（平的）只是语义对应词。

items.example: This road is flatter than that one.
It is the flattest field here.

items.meaning: in a firm or dull way

items.example: The flatness of the plain surprised us.
items.exampleCN: 平原的平坦让我们惊讶。

items.meaning: a person who shares a flat

definition_zh: 视频；录像；录制
definition_en: a recording of moving images, or the medium that carries them
core_image: 手机屏幕上，一段画面正在播放
scene: 面试前她对着手机录了一段自我介绍，反复看了三遍才发出去。 She recorded a short video to introduce herself before the interview.
sceneCN: 这里 video 是「视频、录像」（第 1 个义项：由连续画面构成的影像作品）；句意为面试前她录了一小段视频介绍自己。手机屏幕上正在播放的画面正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 加后缀 -graphy 构成，义为「摄像；录像制作」

senses.title: A recording of moving pictures
senses.definition: a length of recorded moving images, with or without sound
senses.definitionCN: 一段录下的连续画面，可有声音也可无声
senses.example: She recorded a short video to introduce herself before the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 面试前她录了一小段视频介绍自己。
senses.why: Latin video means I see; a recording lets you see again what passed in front of a lens.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 video 意为「我看见」；录像让你再次看见曾经经过镜头的东西。

senses.title: The medium or signal that carries moving pictures
senses.definition: the system, signal, or equipment used to record and show moving images
senses.definitionCN: 用于录制和显示活动影像的系统、信号或设备
senses.example: The lecture was sent to remote students by video.
senses.exampleCN: 这堂课通过视频传给远端的学生。
senses.why: A recording is a thing; the channel that carries it is also called video, as in by video.
senses.whyCN: 录像是一个实物，而承载它的渠道也叫 video，如 by video。

senses.title: Short internet clips and their culture
senses.definition: a short clip made for online sharing, and the stream of such clips
senses.definitionCN: 为网络分享而制作的短片，以及这类内容的整体
senses.example: He spends an hour on short videos every night.
senses.exampleCN: 他每晚都刷一小时短视频。
senses.why: Once clips could be shared in seconds, the word grew into a genre of its own.
senses.whyCN: 短片可以秒速分享之后，这个词发展成了一个独立的内容类别。

senses.title: To record moving images
senses.definition: to make a recording of moving images with a camera or phone
senses.definitionCN: 用摄像机或手机录制活动影像
senses.example: They videoed the whole ceremony on a phone.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用手机把整个仪式都录了下来。
senses.why: Nouns turn into verbs easily in English, and video became one: to video an event.
senses.whyCN: 英语里名词容易转成动词，video 也是如此：把一场活动录下来。

senses.title: In teaching, visual material as a channel
senses.definition: recorded visual material used to teach or demonstrate
senses.definitionCN: 用于教学或示范的录制影像材料
senses.example: The course adds video to every unit.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课每个单元都加入影像材料。
senses.why: Classrooms borrow the word to name visual material that supports a lesson.
senses.whyCN: 课堂借用这个词来称呼辅助教学的影像材料。

intro.en: Video is a modern word taken straight from the Latin verb video, I see.
intro.cn: video 是近代直接取自拉丁动词 video（我看见）的词。

items.en: Videre meant to see, and video is its first person, I see.
items.cn: videre 意为看见，video 是它的第一人称形式「我看见」。

items.en: The Latin phrase video et taceo, I see and keep silent, shows the verb in use.
items.cn: 拉丁语短语 video et taceo（我看见而不语）正是该动词的用例。

items.en: Technical writers of the twentieth century used Latin stems for new media.
items.cn: 二十世纪的技术作者用拉丁词干给新媒介命名。

items.en: Video, from Latin through the sense of seeing, was coined against audio, I hear.
items.cn: video 与表示听见的 audio 相对，借「看见」之义造出。

items.en: It moved from equipment to recording to clips, and then to a verb.
items.cn: 它从设备转到录像，又转到短片，最后成为动词。

note.en: The first group holds compounds built on video, the second the media that compete with it.
note.cn: 第一组是由 video 构成的合成词，第二组是与视频并列的媒介。

entries.definition: magnetic tape for recording pictures
a phone that shows the caller
the making of video recordings
more than one recording
recorded sound
a short piece of a recording
recorded film or video material
a long recorded story on screen

normalIntro.en: Latin video, I see, is the whole story: whatever lets you see again is called video.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁语 video（我看见）就是全部由来：凡是让你再看一遍的东西，都叫 video。

normal.en: Video and audio are a pair: I see against I hear.
normal.cn: video 与 audio 是一对：我看见对我听见。

normal.en: The plural is videos, plainly adding s.
normal.cn: 复数 videos，直接加 s。

normal.en: As a verb it takes -ed: they videoed the event.
normal.cn: 作动词时加 -ed：they videoed the event。

normal.en: Video calling keeps the noun before another noun.
normal.cn: video calling 是名词作定语。

normal.en: The Latin verb videre also gives visible and vision.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 videre 还派生 visible 与 vision。

abstract.en: See a small screen in a hand, a face speaking.
abstract.cn: 想手心里的小屏幕里有一张脸在说话。

abstract.en: Hear the click of a record button.
abstract.cn: 听录制键按下的一声轻响。

abstract.en: Picture a lens and an eye drawn side by side.
abstract.cn: 想一枚镜头和一只眼睛并排放着。

examples.en: The school posted a video of the concert online.
examples.cn: 学校把音乐会的视频发到了网上。

examples.en: Please video the meeting so absent staff can watch.
examples.cn: 请把会议录下来，好让缺席的同事观看。

examples.en: Video has largely replaced tape in newsrooms.
examples.cn: 在新闻编辑室里，视频已基本取代了磁带。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂迪欧」——喂，迪欧，快把刚才那一段录像发给我。

root: 拉丁语 videre（看见）的第一人称 video（我看见）→ 英语 video

sensesIntro.en: From a single Latin sentence, I see, the word grew into recordings, signals, online clips, a verb, and classroom material.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一句拉丁语「我看见」出发，这个词扩展成录像、信号、网络短片、动词与课堂材料。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: moving pictures playing on a phone screen.
core.cn: 核心意象：手机屏幕上播放的活动画面。

branches.en: The recording branch: a self-introduction filmed at home.
branches.cn: 录像分支：家里录的自我介绍。

branches.en: The signal branch: a lecture sent by video.
branches.cn: 信号分支：靠视频传送的课。

branches.en: The feed branch: an hour of short clips.
branches.cn: 信息流分支：刷一小时的短片。

branches.en: The camera branch: filming the whole ceremony.
branches.cn: 镜头分支：录下整场仪式。

branches.en: The classroom branch: video added to a unit.
branches.cn: 课堂分支：单元里加入影像。

intro.en: The Latin root vid-, vis- means to see; video is the bare verb form used as a noun.
intro.cn: 拉丁词根 vid-、vis- 意为看见，video 是直接用作名词的动词形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre, to see, gives video, visible, vision, and television; the root appears whole in this word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre（看见）派生 video、visible、vision、television，本词中词根完整呈现。

items.exampleCN: vid- 在 video 中意为看见。
videotape 由 video 与 tape 合成。

items.example: Audio is the hearing partner of video.
items.exampleCN: audio 是 video 的听觉对应词。

definition_zh: 类别；种类；范畴
definition_en: a group of people or things that share a particular quality, or a basic class in philosophy and logic
core_image: 把一大堆东西分进贴着标签的格子
scene: 评委把参赛作品分成几组。 Each entry was placed in a different category.
sceneCN: 这里 category 指「类别」（第 1 个义项：按共同特点划分的一组）；句意是每件参赛作品都被归入不同的类别。

senses.title: A class of similar things
senses.definition: a group of people or things that share a common feature and are treated together
senses.definitionCN: 具有共同特点、被放在一起处理的一组人或物
senses.example: These films belong to the same category.
senses.exampleCN: 这些影片属于同一类别。
senses.why: The Greek word was a public statement about what something is, and naming a class is exactly that kind of statement.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语源词是对某物是什么的公开断言，而给一个类别命名正是这种断言。

senses.title: A basic class in logic
senses.definition: one of the most general classes used to analyse reality, such as quantity, quality or relation
senses.definitionCN: 用于分析现实的最普遍类别，如数量、性质或关系
senses.example: Kant listed twelve categories of understanding.
senses.exampleCN: 康德列出了十二个知性范畴。
senses.why: Philosophy takes the everyday class word and raises it to the widest possible divisions of thought.
senses.whyCN: 哲学把日常的类别词提升为思维中最宽泛的划分。

intro.en: Category began as a Greek word for a public accusation, then became the logical term for what can be stated of a thing.
intro.cn: category 最初是希腊语中公开指控的说法，后来成为逻辑学中「关于某物能说什么」的术语。

items.en: Agora was the public assembly, and agoreuein meant to speak in public.
items.cn: 希腊语 agora 指公民大会，agoreuein 意为当众发言。

items.en: Kategoria meant an accusation, a statement made publicly against someone.
items.cn: kategoria 意为指控，即当众针对某人作出的陈述。

items.en: Aristotle used the word for the basic ways something can be predicated, such as quantity or relation.
items.cn: 亚里士多德用该词指述说某物的基本方式，如数量或关系。

items.en: Categoria was borrowed into Latin as a technical term of logic.
items.cn: categoria 作为逻辑学术语被借入拉丁语。

items.en: French categorie carried the logical term into ordinary classification.
items.cn: 法语 categorie 把这个逻辑术语带入日常分类。

items.en: Modern English uses category for any practical grouping, from age groups to product types.
items.cn: 现代英语用 category 指任何实用分组，从年龄组到产品类型。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the classify family, while the meaning group gives other grouping words.
note.cn: 形近组沿分类词族展开，近义组给出其他表示分组的词。

entries.definition: to put things into classes
the act of sorting into classes
stated without conditions or doubt
entries.definitionCN: 无条件、毫不含糊地陈述的

entries.definition: a group of things of the same kind
a kind or sort of person or thing
a set of people or things placed together
entries.definitionCN: 放在一起的一组人或物

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the public-speech root, the -ize and -ical family and the everyday grouping phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用「当众发言」词根、-ize 与 -ical 词族以及日常分组搭配。

normal.en: Category and categorize differ by the -ize ending, which turns the class into an action.
normal.cn: category 与 categorize 只差 -ize 词尾，后者把类别变成动作。

normal.en: The Greek root agora, a public square, also appears in agoraphobia, fear of open spaces.
normal.cn: 希腊语词根 agora（公共广场）也出现在 agoraphobia（广场恐惧）里。

normal.en: Age category and product category show the word doing practical sorting work.
normal.cn: age category 与 product category 展示这个词的实际分组功能。

normal.en: Categorical answers leave no room for doubt, as if the class were fixed for ever.
normal.cn: categorical 的回答不留怀疑余地，仿佛类别已经永久定死。

normal.en: The plural changes y to ies, so one category becomes many categories.
normal.cn: 复数把 y 变成 ies，一个 category 变成许多 categories。

abstract.en: Picture a market square where a speaker names each item aloud.
abstract.cn: 想象集市广场上有人高声给每样东西归类。

abstract.en: Picture a wall of labelled drawers, each holding one kind of thing.
abstract.cn: 想象一面贴着标签的抽屉墙，每格只放一类东西。

abstract.en: Picture a judge sorting cards into neat piles on a desk.
abstract.cn: 想象裁判在桌上把卡片分成整齐的几堆。

examples.en: The prize has a separate category for young writers.
examples.cn: 该奖项为年轻作者单设一个类别。

examples.en: Books in this category sell quickly.
examples.cn: 这一类别的书卖得很快。

examples.en: Please categorize the files by date.
examples.cn: 请按日期把文件分类。

dict_mnemonic.text: category 里有 cate 加 gory：想象把东西按标签排成一排排格子，每一格就是一个类别。

root: 源自希腊语 kategoria（公开指控、断言），由 kata（针对）与 agoreuein（当众发言）构成，经拉丁语与法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: A public statement about what something is becomes a logical class, then any practical grouping of things.
sensesIntro.cn: 关于某物是什么的公开断言变成逻辑类别，再变成任何实用的分组。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a labelled slot into which similar things are sorted.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个贴着标签、用来归放同类物的格子。

branches.en: Philosophy keeps the widest classes of predication.
branches.cn: 哲学保留了最宽泛的述谓类别。

branches.en: Everyday use narrows the class to any group sharing a feature.
branches.cn: 日常用法把类别收窄为任何共享某一特点的组。

branches.en: Age category and product category apply the grouping to people and goods.
branches.cn: 年龄组与产品类别把分组用到人和货物上。

branches.en: Both senses answer the question of what kind of thing something is.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在回答「这属于哪一种东西」。

branches.en: The logical sense stays technical and mostly appears in philosophy.
branches.cn: 逻辑义偏技术性，多出现在哲学文本中。

intro.en: Category builds verbs and nouns with -ize and -ization, and an adjective with -ical.
intro.cn: category 用 -ize、-ization 构成动词与名词，用 -ical 构成形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin categoria preserved the Greek term of logic, which French later passed to English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 categoria 保留了希腊语逻辑术语，法语后来把它传给英语。

items.exampleCN: kategoria 经亚里士多德进入逻辑学。
agora 藏在 kategoria 之中。

latinEntries.example: Categoria passed from Greek into Latin.
latinEntries.exampleCN: categoria 从希腊语进入拉丁语。

definition_zh: 建造；施工；建筑物；构造
definition_en: the process of building something, or the way something is put together
core_image: 围着绿色围栏的工地，塔吊在缓慢转动
scene: 街角的旧楼被围了起来，里面传出敲打声。 The new library is still under construction.
sceneCN: 这里 construction 指「建造、施工」（第 1 个义项：把材料建成建筑的过程）；句意是新图书馆仍在施工中。

senses.title: The work of building
senses.definition: the process of putting materials together to make a building
senses.definitionCN: 把材料拼合成建筑的过程
senses.example: The bridge is still under construction.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥仍在施工中。
senses.why: A site is a promise that is not finished yet.
senses.whyCN: 一个工地就是一个还没兑现的承诺。

senses.title: A built thing
senses.definition: a structure that has been built, often a large one
senses.definitionCN: 已经建成的结构物，常指较大的建筑
senses.example: The old construction beside the river was pulled down.
senses.exampleCN: 河边那座旧建筑被拆掉了。
senses.why: Once finished, the work becomes a thing with a shadow.
senses.whyCN: 活儿干完，就变成一个会投下影子的东西。

senses.title: The way parts fit
senses.definition: the arrangement of words or parts inside a whole
senses.definitionCN: 词语或部件在整体内部的排列方式
senses.example: The grammar book explains this construction clearly.
senses.exampleCN: 这本语法书把这个结构讲得很清楚。
senses.why: Sentences are also assembled, and their frames can be named.
senses.whyCN: 句子也是装配起来的，它们的架子也能被命名。

intro.en: Construction comes from Latin constructio, a piling together, from construere, to build up.
intro.cn: construction 来自拉丁语 constructio，意为堆在一起，源自 construere（建造）。

items.en: Struere meant to pile or lay in layers.
items.cn: struere 意为堆积或层层铺放。

items.en: Construere meant to pile materials into a building.
items.cn: construere 意为把材料堆成建筑。

items.en: Constructio named both building work and the fitting of words.
items.cn: constructio 同时指建造工作与词语的搭配。

items.en: French construction kept those two sides together.
items.cn: 法语 construction 把这两面保留在一起。

items.en: English construction first meant the act of building.
items.cn: 英语 construction 最初指建造的行为。

items.en: It now also means a structure and a grammatical pattern.
items.cn: 如今它也指建筑物与语法结构。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin pile base struct-, and the meaning group names other words for a built whole.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语堆积词基 struct-，近义组列出其他表示建成之物的词。

entries.definition: to build something from separate parts
meant to help improve something
information that tells you how to do something
a structure with walls and a roof
something that has been built or arranged
the fitting together of separate parts

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a fenced site with a crane, then move to the finished building and to the frame inside a sentence.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从围起来的工地与塔吊开始，再到建成的楼房，最后到句子内部的架子。

normal.en: Con- is together and struct is pile, so construction is the act of piling parts together.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，struct 是堆，construction 就是把部件堆到一起的行为。

normal.en: Under construction means the promise is still open.
normal.cn: 正在施工，意思是那个承诺还开着口。

normal.en: Every building is a construction, and so is every well-made sentence.
normal.cn: 每栋楼都是建造物，每个搭得好的句子也是。

normal.en: The crane turns, and the skyline changes by one beam.
normal.cn: 塔吊转一圈，天际线就多一根梁。

normal.en: Watch the frame, not the paint.
normal.cn: 看骨架，不要看油漆。

abstract.en: Picture a green fence around a hole in the ground.
abstract.cn: 想象一圈绿色围栏围着一个土坑。

abstract.en: Picture a crane lifting a beam against grey sky.
abstract.cn: 想象塔吊在灰天里吊起一根梁。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence drawn as a frame of boxes.
abstract.cn: 想象一个句子被画成一排方框的架子。

examples.en: The road is closed because of construction work.
examples.cn: 这条路因施工而封闭。

examples.en: A new hospital is under construction outside the city.
examples.cn: 城外正在建一所新医院。

examples.en: This construction appears often in formal writing.
examples.cn: 这个结构在正式写作中经常出现。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 construction 记成 con（一起）加 struct（堆积）加 ion：把材料一起堆叠起来的过程，就是建造。

root: 源自拉丁语 constructio（堆叠、建造），词根 construere 由 com（一起）与 struere（堆积）构成，后指建造过程、建筑物与语法构造。

sensesIntro.en: From a site where a crane turns, to the building that finally stands, and to the frame hidden inside a sentence.
sensesIntro.cn: 从塔吊转动的工地，到最终立起来的楼房，最后到藏在句子里的架子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fenced site where a crane lifts beam after beam.
core.cn: 核心意象：围起来的工地上，塔吊一根根吊起钢梁。

branches.en: The first sense is the noisy work that is not yet finished.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是尚未完工的、喧闹的活儿。

branches.en: The second sense is the thing that remains when the noise stops.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是噪音停下后留下的东西。

branches.en: The third sense is a frame of words rather than of steel.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是词语而非钢梁搭成的架子。

branches.en: Both senses point to the same site, one before and one after.
branches.cn: 两个义项指向同一个工地，一个在之前，一个在之后。

branches.en: A building and a sentence both hold their shape by design.
branches.cn: 楼房与句子都靠设计守住自己的形状。

intro.en: Construction is built on Latin con-, together, plus struere, to pile, with the noun ending -ion.
intro.cn: construction 由拉丁语 con-（一起）、struere（堆积）与名词词尾 -ion 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin pile base struct- also appears in structure, instruct and destruction.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的堆积词基 struct- 也出现在 structure、instruct 与 destruction 中。

definition_zh: 部门；系；百货商店的专柜区
definition_en: one of the parts into which a large organization is divided
core_image: 一栋大楼的平面图被切成许多小格，每格亮着一盏灯
scene: 商场二楼挂满衣服，三楼摆着锅碗，指示牌把每层分成几块。 She works in the sales department of a small company.
sceneCN: 这里 department 指「部门」（第 1 个义项：大机构划分出的部分）；句意是她在小公司的销售部工作。

pos.zh: 部门；系；百货商店的专柜区

senses.title: A division of an organization
senses.definition: one of the parts into which a large organization is divided
senses.definitionCN: 大机构被划分成的部分之一
senses.example: She works in the sales department of a small company.
senses.exampleCN: 她在小公司的销售部工作。
senses.why: When an organization grows past one table, it begins to cut itself into parts.
senses.whyCN: 当一个机构一张桌子坐不下，它就开始把自己切成几块。

senses.title: A subject area at a university
senses.definition: a group of teachers and courses in one subject
senses.definitionCN: 同一学科的老师与课程组成的单位
senses.example: She teaches in the history department.
senses.exampleCN: 她在历史系任教。
senses.why: A university is also too large for one voice, so it divides by subject.
senses.whyCN: 大学也大到容不下一个声音，于是按学科分开。

senses.title: A section of a large shop
senses.definition: one of the areas of a large shop that sells a kind of goods
senses.definitionCN: 大商店里售卖某一类商品的区域
senses.example: The store has a whole department for kitchen goods.
senses.exampleCN: 这家商店有一整块区域卖厨房用品。
senses.why: A shop that sells everything must sort itself like a small city.
senses.whyCN: 什么都卖的商店，得像座小城那样把自己归类。

intro.en: Department came from French département, which grew out of départir, to divide or share out.
intro.cn: department 来自法语 département，而它又由 départir（划分、分配）长出来。

items.en: Departement came from departir, to divide or share out.
items.cn: departement 来自 departir，意为划分或分配。

items.en: The word named an administrative division of the state.
items.cn: 这个词指国家的行政区划。

items.en: English took department for a branch of government or business.
items.cn: 英语借来 department，指政府或企业的分支。

items.en: Universities and shops borrowed it for their own divisions.
items.cn: 大学与商店也借它来称呼自己的分区。

items.en: Now any large body can be cut into departments.
items.cn: 如今任何大的机构都能被切成部门。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the depart stem, and the meaning group gives three words for a part of something larger.
note.cn: 形近组共用 depart 词干，近义组则给出三个表示「大东西的一部分」的词。

entries.definition: to leave a place
the act of leaving a place
relating to one department
a part of a large organization
one of the parts something is cut into
entries.definitionCN: 某物被分成的部分之一

entries.definition: a local office of a larger body

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a floor plan cut into rooms and end with a shop that sorts everything by kind.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从被切成一个个房间的平面图开始，落到按类别整理万物的商店。

normal.en: A department is a slice of a big building.
normal.cn: 部门就是一栋大楼切下来的一片。

normal.en: The sign on the door tells you which slice you are in.
normal.cn: 门上的牌子告诉你，你在哪一片里。

normal.en: A university divides by subject, a shop by goods.
normal.cn: 大学按学科分，商店按货物分。

normal.en: Department and departure share the same parting root.
normal.cn: department 与 departure 共用同一个「分开」的词根。

normal.en: Too many people in one room is how departments begin.
normal.cn: 一间屋子挤了太多人，部门就是这样开始的。

abstract.en: Picture a map of a building with each room lit a different colour.
abstract.cn: 想象一张楼内地图，每个房间亮着不同颜色。

abstract.en: Picture a long corridor with names painted above every door.
abstract.cn: 想象一条长走廊，每扇门上方都刷着名字。

abstract.en: Picture shelves sorted until nothing is out of place.
abstract.cn: 想象货架被整理到没有一样东西放错。

examples.en: She works in the sales department of a small company.
examples.cn: 她在小公司的销售部工作。

examples.en: She teaches in the history department.
examples.cn: 她在历史系任教。

examples.en: The store has a whole department for kitchen goods.
examples.cn: 这家商店有一整块区域卖厨房用品。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 department 记成「地面切成块」：de 是分开，part 是部分，一个大机构被分成一块块，就是部门。

root: 来自法语 département，源头是 départir（划分、分配）。它先指国家的行政区划，十八世纪进入英语后指政府或企业的分支，十九世纪又被大学与商店借去称呼各自的划分。

sensesIntro.en: From an office divided by function, to a university divided by subject, to a shop divided by goods.
sensesIntro.cn: 从按职能划分的办公室，到按学科划分的大学，再到按货物划分的商店。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a floor plan cut into rooms, each with its own lamp.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张被切成房间的平面图，每间亮着自己的灯。

branches.en: The first sense is work cut into manageable parts.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是把工作切成管得过来的几块。

branches.en: The second sense is knowledge cut by subject.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是把知识按学科切开。

branches.en: The third sense is goods cut by kind.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是把货物按种类分开。

branches.en: An office and a university both divide because one voice cannot hold everything.
branches.cn: 办公室与大学都要划分，因为一个声音装不下所有事。

branches.en: A subject and a shelf are both sorting devices.
branches.cn: 学科与货架，都是分类的工具。

intro.en: Department belongs to the parting family and carries the idea of division into organized life.
intro.cn: department 属于「分开」这一族，把划分的观念带进组织生活。

latinIntro.en: The base is partire, to divide, seen also in part and partial.
latinIntro.cn: 它的词基是 partire（划分），在 part 与 partial 里也能看到。

items.meaning: a part of a large organization
items.example: She works in the sales department.
The departmental meeting is at nine.

他们把整个办公室按部门划分了。

items.meaning: a large shop with many sections
items.example: The department store opens at nine.

definition_zh: 暴力的；猛烈的；剧烈的
definition_en: using or involving force meant to hurt, or happening with great force
core_image: 被人一把推开的门，撞在墙上反弹回来
scene: 电影里两个人争执起来，其中一个一把把桌子掀翻，杯子全摔在地上。 The argument turned violent before anyone could stop it.
sceneCN: 这里 violent 是「暴力的」（第 1 个义项：涉及意在伤害他人的武力）；句意为还没人来得及阻止，争吵就演变成暴力冲突。被掀翻的桌子与砸碎的杯子正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 去后缀 -ent 构成的名词，义为「暴力」
加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「猛烈地」
加前缀 non- 构成，义为「非暴力的」

senses.title: Using force to hurt people
senses.definition: using physical force intended to injure or kill
senses.definitionCN: 使用意在伤害或杀害他人的体力
senses.example: The argument turned violent before anyone could stop it.
senses.exampleCN: 还没人来得及阻止，争吵就演变成了暴力冲突。
senses.why: A violent act is force aimed at a body, and the sentence usually shows a body receiving it.
senses.whyCN: 暴力行为是针对人体施加的力量，句子里往往能看到承受的那具身体。

senses.title: Happening with great natural force
senses.definition: of weather or natural events, striking with great power
senses.definitionCN: 天气或自然现象以巨大力量袭来
senses.example: A violent storm closed the harbour for two days.
senses.exampleCN: 一场猛烈的风暴让港口停摆两天。
senses.why: Nature strikes with the same force as a fist, so the adjective crosses over.
senses.whyCN: 自然的力量与拳头一样，形容词因此跨了过来。

senses.title: Extremely strong in feeling
senses.definition: of feelings, reactions, or changes, very strong and sudden
senses.definitionCN: 指情感、反应或变化非常强烈而突然
senses.example: He had a violent dislike of being interrupted.
senses.exampleCN: 他极其厌恶被人打断。
senses.why: A feeling that arrives with force takes the adjective of force, even without any blow.
senses.whyCN: 猛然涌来的情绪也用了表示力量的那个形容词，即便没有任何一击。

senses.title: In law, involving force against a person
senses.definition: of a crime, committed with force against a person
senses.definitionCN: 指犯罪时对人使用了强制
senses.example: He was charged with violent robbery.
senses.exampleCN: 他被控暴力抢劫。
senses.why: Law separates crimes with force from those without, and the adjective does that work.
senses.whyCN: 法律把带强制的犯罪与不带强制的分开，这个形容词正承担这一区分。

senses.title: In colour or light, very intense
senses.definition: of colour, extremely bright and harsh to the eye
senses.definitionCN: 指颜色极其鲜明、刺眼
senses.example: A violent orange covered the whole wall.
senses.exampleCN: 整面墙刷成了刺眼的橘色。
senses.why: Strong colour hits the eye the way a blow hits the body, so the sense extends.
senses.whyCN: 强烈的颜色冲击眼睛，如同打击冲击身体，词义由此延伸。

intro.en: Violent comes from Latin violentia, the quality of force.
intro.cn: violent 来自拉丁语 violentia，指力量的性质。

items.en: Vis was force, and violentus described one full of it.
items.cn: vis 是力量，violentus 形容充满力量的人。

items.en: The adjective came before the English noun, both from the same stem.
items.cn: 形容词先于英语名词出现，二者同出一词干。

items.en: French violent passed the adjective into English.
items.cn: 法语 violent 把形容词传入英语。

items.en: English used it for blows, storms, and heated speech.
items.cn: 中世纪英语用它指打击、风暴与激烈的言辞。

items.en: Colour and reaction senses joined in later centuries.
items.cn: 色彩与反应等义项在之后的世纪加入。

note.en: The first group holds the violent family, the second the adjectives for force, rage, and calm.
note.cn: 第一组是 violent 词族，第二组是力量、愤怒与平静的形容词。

normalIntro.en: The ending -ent marks the adjective; the stem marks the force.
normalIntro.cn: 词尾 -ent 标记形容词，词干标记力量。

normal.en: Drop -ent and add -ence for the noun violence.
normal.cn: 去掉 -ent 加 -ence 得名词 violence。

normal.en: Add -ly for violently, with force in the manner.

normal.en: Nonviolent puts non- in front to deny the force.
normal.cn: nonviolent 前置 non- 以否定力量。

normal.en: The second syllable is weak: VI-o-lent.

abstract.en: Picture an orange too bright to look at.
abstract.cn: 想一片亮得刺眼的橘色。
